questions.question: On a related list, which buttons are commonly used for managing the records on the list?
questions.explanation: On a related list, the New button creates a new related record, and the Edit button opens a list editor for inline editing of existing records. 'Add' is not a standard related list button, 'Manage' is not available, and 'Publish' is unrelated to related lists.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is true about Column Context Menus?
options: It displays actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data
It displays actions related to filtering options, assigning tags, and search
It displays actions related to viewing and filtering the entire list
It displays actions such as view form, view related task, and add relationship
questions.explanation: The Column Context Menu appears when you right-click a column header. It provides actions like creating quick reports, configuring the list (show/hide columns), and exporting data. The other options describe the Title Bar context menu or the row-level context menu.

questions.question: When looking at a long list of records, you want to quickly filter to show only those with Category of Hardware. How might you do that?
options: On the Category column header, right click and select Show > Hardware
Right click on magnifier, type Hardware and click enter
On the list, locate and right click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching
On Breadcrumb, click > icon, type Hardware and click enter
Click Funnel icon, type Hardware and click enter
questions.explanation: Right-clicking on a specific value in a list column (like 'Hardware') and selecting Show Matching instantly filters the list to show only records with that value. This is the quickest way to filter without using the filter builder or breadcrumbs.

questions.question: Which modules can you use to create a new table?
questions.explanation: You can create new tables using the Tables module (System Definition > Tables) and the Tables and Columns module. Schema map is for viewing relationships, and 'Database applications' is not a valid ServiceNow module.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a database setting on the application access section of a table?
questions.explanation: Application Access controls on a table include Can create, Can update, Can delete, and Can read. There is no 'Can write' — it's not a valid database setting. Write operations are covered by 'Can create' and 'Can update'.

questions.question: A task worker asks how they can monitor any updates occurring to records assigned to them. What do you suggest?
options: On My Work list, select the Activity Stream icon to show a frame with live updates
Click on the eyeglass icon to expand the Monitor frame
Open an Agent Workspace tab for each record
questions.explanation: The Activity Stream icon on the My Work list shows a live feed of updates occurring on records assigned to you. It provides real-time visibility into changes without needing to open each record individually.

questions.question: What will happen if you click 'Show matching' on the software category on the incident list?
options: All incidents with the software category will remain visible.
The list will display all categories except software.
questions.explanation: Show Matching is a list filter action that keeps only records matching the selected value visible. So clicking 'Show matching' on the software category retains only incidents categorized as Software, filtering out all other categories.

questions.question: On the form header, which element do you use to access form templates?
questions.explanation: Form templates are accessed via the More options (...) menu on the form header (also called the hamburger or context menu). It provides options like Save as Template, Apply Template, Configure Form, etc.

questions.question: The report designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to adjust the look of your report including colors, titles, and legend layout?
questions.explanation: The Style section in the report designer controls the visual appearance — colors, chart titles, legend position and layout, fonts, and other formatting options. The Data section handles source/filters, and Type handles chart type.

questions.question: What happens if you select 'Publish' when creating articles manually or by import?
options: It triggers the publish workflow assigned to the knowledge base.
It sends an email to the administrator.
It exports the article to a PDF.
questions.explanation: When you click Publish on a knowledge article, it triggers the publish workflow assigned to that knowledge base. This workflow may include approval steps before the article becomes publicly visible.

questions.question: Which module would you use to create a new automation of business logic such as approvals, tasks, and notifications?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer (Process Automation > Flow Designer) is the modern, no-code/low-code tool for building automated processes including approvals, tasks, notifications, and integrations. Workflow Editor is the legacy tool.

questions.question: Which tab on the knowledge base record would you use to identify the sets of users who are able to read articles in that knowledge base?
questions.explanation: The Can Read tab on a knowledge base record defines which user criteria (roles, groups, users) have read access to articles in that knowledge base. This controls article visibility for different audiences.

questions.question: What sections do you need to fill in when creating a notification?
questions.explanation: A notification requires three key sections: Who will receive (recipients), When to send (trigger conditions/events), and What it will contain (email body/template). 'Who will send' and 'Notes' are not standard notification sections.

questions.question: Knowledge base search results can be sorted by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Knowledge base search results can be sorted by Relevance (text match quality), Views (most viewed articles), and Newest (most recently created). 'Popularity' and 'My group articles' are not standard sort options.

questions.question: What ServiceNow feature can be triggered by events and is used to inform users about activities or updates in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Notifications are the ServiceNow feature triggered by events to inform users about activities or updates. Events generate notifications, Business Rules automate server-side logic, and Alerts are a different feature for monitoring.

questions.question: The report designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to specify the name of the report and the table or data source?
questions.explanation: The Data section in the report designer is where you specify the report name, select the source table, and configure data filters. It defines what data the report pulls from.

questions.question: While showing a customer their incident form, they ask to change the priority field title to display their internal terminology. How would you do that?
options: Right click on Priority and select Configure Dictionary
Right click on Priority and select Configure Label
Right click on Priority and select Configure Display Settings
Right click on Priority and select Configure Column
questions.explanation: To change a field label, you can right-click the field and select either Configure Dictionary (to change the column label at the dictionary level) or Configure Label (to change only the display label on the form). Both approaches work.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about sys_dictionary?
options: It is a table where all the details about the fields are stored.
It is used to run client scripts.
questions.explanation: sys_dictionary is the system table that stores metadata about all fields (columns) in ServiceNow — including field type, max length, default value, reference, and other attributes. It's the core schema definition table.

questions.question: You will see a text area widget where you can add __________ to your ACL. It is known as:
questions.explanation: The text area widget in an ACL rule where you define conditions is called Conditional Expressions. It allows you to specify when the ACL should apply using field-based conditions without scripting.

questions.question: In a workflow, what is the workflow timeline?
options: Defines unique key for record. If record found, import will update the record. If not found, import will create a new record.
Shows the progress of a workflow. It provides a complete time-based display of activities associated with workflow context.
An automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities.
questions.explanation: The Workflow Timeline shows the progress of a workflow context. It provides a complete time-based display of all activities — approvals, tasks, conditions — that have been executed, along with timestamps and durations.

questions.question: What does a request number in the service catalog represent?
options: It represents the individual item in the order
It represents the task to complete
questions.explanation: In the ServiceNow Service Catalog, a Request (REQ) number represents the overall order placed by the user. Each request can contain one or more Requested Items (RITMs), which represent individual items, and Catalog Tasks (SCTASKs), which represent tasks to fulfill the request.

questions.question: An outbound SOAP message is defined. Which function can invoke the SOAP message?
questions.explanation: A UI Action (such as a button, link, or context menu item) can invoke an outbound SOAP message. UI Actions run server-side scripts when clicked, making them ideal for triggering web service calls on demand. Script Includes store reusable functions but aren't directly invocable by users. Business Rules trigger on record operations, and UI Policies are client-side — neither is designed to let users manually invoke outbound SOAP calls.

questions.question: Which statement describes the contents of the CMDB?
options: The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets
The CMDB contains the Business Rules that direct the intangible, configurable assets used by a company
The CMDB archives all Service Management PaaS equipment metadata and usage statistics
The CMDB contains ITIL process data pertaining to configuration items
questions.explanation: The CMDB contains data about both tangible assets (servers, laptops) and intangible business services (email service, HR portal). It maps the relationships between all configuration items.

questions.question: What can be performed by an inbound email action?
questions.explanation: Inbound email actions can automatically create or update task records when emails matching specific conditions are received by the instance.

questions.question: What is a true characteristic for workflows in the service catalog?
options: The start & end activities in workflows can be changed
Workflows can have a maximum of five rounds of approval actions
Only one rollback activity is allowed in a workflow
Workflows can have multiple rounds of approval actions
questions.explanation: Workflows in the service catalog can have multiple rounds of approval actions. Start and end activities cannot be changed, and there's no limit on rollback activities.

questions.question: Which statement is true for a field on an audited table?
options: Add "no_audit = true" to attribute for exclude from auditing
Add "no_audit = 0" to attribute for exclude from auditing
questions.explanation: To exclude a specific field from auditing on an audited table, add no_audit = true to the field's attributes. This prevents changes to that field from being logged.

questions.question: Which application menu has details about system upgrades?
questions.explanation: The Upgrade History module (System Diagnostics > Upgrade History) shows details about system upgrades, including versions, dates, and any conflicts encountered.

questions.question: What components make up the knowledge process?
options: Document creation, approval and review from SMEs and publishing
Document creation, approval and review from SMEs
questions.explanation: The knowledge process consists of document creation, approval and review from SMEs (Subject Matter Experts), and publishing. This ensures quality control before articles go live.

questions.question: What is any content created using the ServiceNow knowledge base?
questions.explanation: Content created in the ServiceNow knowledge base is called an Article. Articles are organized within knowledge bases and can be versioned, reviewed, and published.

questions.question: Where is business rule information stored in a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: Business rule scripts are stored in the sys_script table. sys_script_include stores script includes, and sys_include is not a standard ServiceNow table.

questions.question: Where is Mid server communication saved?
questions.explanation: MID Server communications are saved in the ECC Queue (External Communication Channel). It handles all inbound and outbound messages between the instance and MID Server.

questions.question: Can only predefined roles be migrated from one instance to another?
questions.explanation: Both predefined and custom roles can be migrated between instances using update sets. The statement is False.

questions.question: When searching using the app navigator search field, what can be returned?
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator search returns application names, module names, combined application/module names, and favorites. History records are not returned in navigator search.

questions.question: In an SLA, what attribute controls what is calculated as hours in a workday or work week?
questions.explanation: The Schedule attribute in an SLA defines business hours — what counts as working time. It determines how hours in a workday/week are calculated for SLA tracking.

questions.question: What enables you to track and aggregate data over time through elements called scorecards and indicators?
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics tracks and aggregates data over time using scorecards (collections of indicators) and indicators (KPI metrics). It enables trend analysis and goal tracking.

questions.question: Choose all possible ways by which a service catalog workflow can be attached.
questions.explanation: A service catalog workflow can be attached automatically based on conditions or manually on the catalog item form. Transform maps are for data imports, not catalog workflows.

questions.question: What are tables that exist in the base system called?
questions.explanation: Tables that exist in the base system (out-of-the-box) are called core tables. Custom tables start with 'u_' prefix, and there's no category called 'default' or 'fixed' tables.

questions.question: On access control definitions, what are ways you can set the permissions on a table?
options: Script that sets the answer variable to true or false
questions.explanation: ACL permissions can be set using Roles (who), Conditional Expressions (when), and Groups (which group). CRUD refers to operations, not permission types.

questions.question: When designing a relationship between two configuration items, which of the following will be the base CI?
options: The base CI can be the parent or child CI depending on the relationship nature
The relationship doesn't involve parent-child roles
The base CI will be the parent CI
The base CI will be the child CI
questions.explanation: When designing a CI relationship, the base CI is the child CI. The relationship is defined from the perspective of the base CI looking up to its parent.

questions.question: The Employee On-boarding team has asked for a way for managers to order computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones for new employees. How would you proceed?
questions.explanation: An Order Guide groups multiple catalog items into a single order, perfect for bundling computers, monitors, and business cards into one manager request.

questions.question: Which field type displays as a checkbox on the Form?
questions.explanation: True/False and Checkbox field types both display as checkboxes on a form. Choice displays as a dropdown, and Multiselect/Checkbox list show multiple selections differently.

questions.question: What happens when you change the order of columns using the Column Context Menu > Configure > List Layout?
options: The order of columns for this list changes for all users
The order of columns for this list changes only for the logged-in user
The order of columns for this list changes for all users except the users who personalized the list
questions.explanation: Using Column Context Menu > Configure > List Layout changes the column order for all users. This is an admin-level change, unlike Personalize List which affects only the current user.

questions.question: Which resource would you use to determine if a specific user could contribute to a particular knowledge base?
questions.explanation: User Criteria Diagnostics lets you check if a specific user meets the criteria to contribute to a knowledge base. It evaluates all user criteria rules and shows the results.

questions.question: Business rules are real time.
questions.explanation: Business rules are not real-time — they are server-side scripts that execute when records are displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or when a table is queried. They run asynchronously or on database operations.

questions.question: ServiceNow provides customers with a dedicated database, application and data isolation using which model?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow provides single-tenant architecture — each customer gets a dedicated database and application instance, ensuring complete data isolation and security.

questions.question: How can administrators utilise the same content for different notification channels?
questions.explanation: Administrators can use common notification content to share the same content across different notification channels (email, SMS, push). This avoids duplicating content for each channel.

questions.question: Which fields can be configured in reporting to perform arithmetic, coalesce, concatenation and length?
questions.explanation: Function fields in reporting allow arithmetic operations, coalesce, concatenation, and length calculations. They enable computed columns in reports.

questions.question: How can administrators personalize access to applications and modules for users and groups in the Platform?
options: Create homepages and dashboards and assign specific work to users and groups
Create a workspace with links to access the applications and modules
Configure sidebars with links, specific to users and groups
Enable the user preference to specify the page that appears when they log in
questions.explanation: Admins can personalize Platform access using homepages/dashboards, workspaces with links, and custom menus. These allow role-specific views and quick access to relevant apps.

questions.question: Users with the following role will have full view/edit/delete and share privileges of all dashboards on given ServiceNow instance.
questions.explanation: The dashboard_admin role provides full view, edit, delete, and share privileges for all dashboards. Other roles like report_admin or homepage_admin have more limited scope.

questions.question: To retrieve an update set from a remote instance, navigate to:
options: All > System Update Sets > Update Sources
All > System Update Sets > Retrieved Sources
All > System Update Sets > Committed Sources
questions.explanation: To retrieve update sets from a remote instance, navigate to System Update Sets > Update Sources. This is where you configure and pull from remote instance connections.

questions.question: As an IT employee, what interface would you use to browse internal IT documentation like troubleshooting scripts and FAQs?
questions.explanation: The Knowledge application (Self-Service > Knowledge) is the interface for browsing internal IT documentation, troubleshooting guides, and other knowledge articles.

questions.question: What are the three key tables in an enterprise CMDB?
questions.explanation: The three key CMDB tables are: cmdb (base table), cmdb_ci (configuration items extending cmdb), and cmdb_rel_ci (relationships between CIs).

questions.question: Your customer would like to create a new template to notify users who are affected by network outages. Which module would you use?
questions.explanation: To create a notification template for network outages, navigate to System Notification > Email > Notifications. This is the standard module for creating and managing all email notifications.

questions.question: On a filter condition, which component is always a choice list?
questions.explanation: On a filter condition, the Operator is always a choice list (e.g., 'is', 'is not', 'contains', 'starts with'). The field and value components vary based on context.

questions.question: A Role is defined as what?
options: A set of user access policies
A set of access control rules
questions.explanation: A Role is defined as a collection of permissions. Roles bundle multiple access rights together, making it easy to assign consistent access levels to users.

questions.question: If a knowledge base has no access details specified, what users are able to read articles?
options: Any user with an article's permalink
questions.explanation: If no access details are specified on a knowledge base, any active user can read articles. Access restrictions only apply when User Criteria is explicitly configured.

questions.question: What catalog tool would you use to create a catalog item or record producer?
questions.explanation: The Catalog Builder is the modern tool for creating catalog items and record producers. It provides a guided, visual interface for building service catalog offerings.

questions.question: What is common between CIs, Users, Groups?
options: Any changes to these are not captured in an update set
sys_db_object is parent of all tables
All changes to these are captured in an update set
They are stored in the same base table cmdb
questions.explanation: CIs, Users, and Groups are all data records — changes to data are NOT captured in update sets. Only configuration changes (forms, scripts, workflows) are tracked in update sets.

questions.question: From the Service Catalog, what are examples of tables having a one to many relationship?
options: One Request can have many Requested Items
One Requested Item can have many Catalog Tasks
One Requested Item can have many Approvals
One Approval can have many Requests
One Cart can have many Requests
questions.explanation: In the Service Catalog: one Request → many Requested Items, one Requested Item → many Catalog Tasks, and one Requested Item → many Approvals. These are the standard one-to-many relationships.

questions.question: In what order are Access Controls evaluated?
options: Table-level most specific to most general; then Field-level most specific to most general
Field-level most specific to most general; then Table-level most specific to most general
Field-level most general to most specific; then Row-level most specific to most general
Table-level most specific to most general, then Row-level most specific to most general
questions.explanation: ACLs are evaluated table-level first (most specific to most general), then field-level. This means a table-specific ACL is checked before inherited table ACLs, then field-level rules apply.

questions.question: What is the name of the string that displays filter criteria?
questions.explanation: The Breadcrumb is the string displayed above a list that shows the current filter criteria in a human-readable format (e.g., 'State is Open AND Priority is 1 - Critical'). The Filter bar is where you build conditions, but the breadcrumb displays the active filter criteria. Context menus and column headers serve different purposes.

questions.question: Virtual Agent capabilities include which three of the following?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent capabilities include: Performing diagnostics (running automated troubleshooting steps), Providing tutorial/how-to information (guiding users through processes), and Answering FAQs (resolving common questions instantly). Virtual Agent cannot translate conversations between languages or perform elevated role functions — those require human intervention or separate tools.

questions.question: Which features allow you to update multiple records at one time?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, E: Update Selected Action and List Editor. Options like "Bulk Record Update" and "Data Remediation Dashboard" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: How can the abbreviation CSDM be expanded?
questions.explanation: CSDM stands for Common Service Data Model. It is ServiceNow's standard framework for organizing service-related data in the CMDB. CSDM defines how business services, technical services, and their supporting CIs should be structured and related, providing a consistent data architecture across the platform.

questions.question: An order from the Service Catalog has been placed. Two records are created. Which two records are associated with this newly ordered item?
questions.explanation: When a Service Catalog order is placed, two records are created: a Requested Item [sc_req_item] representing the specific item ordered, and a Catalog Task [sc_task] for the fulfillment work. A parent Request [sc_request] is also created as the order container. Change Requests and Problem Tasks are part of different ITSM processes, not catalog ordering.

questions.question: A customer wants to use a client script to validate things on a form to make sure the submission makes sense. What type of client script would you recommend?
questions.explanation: For validating form submissions, an onSubmit Client Script is recommended. It runs when the user clicks Save/Submit/Update and can validate field values before the record is saved. If validation fails, it returns false to cancel the submission. onLoad runs when the form opens (too early for validation), and onChange runs when fields change (not at submission time).

questions.question: Which ServiceNow products can be used to discover and populate the CMDB?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow products for discovering and populating the CMDB include Discovery (agent-based scanning of network infrastructure) and IntegrationHub ETL (Extract, Transform, Load for importing CI data from external sources). Finder and CMDB Integration Dashboard are not standard CMDB population tools.

questions.question: Which system property is added and set to true in order to see impersonation events in the System Log?
questions.explanation: The system property glide.sys.log_impersonation must be added and set to true to log impersonation events in the System Log. This enables audit tracking of who impersonated whom and what actions were taken. Other property names like glide.impersonation_setting or glide.sys.all_impersonation are not valid ServiceNow properties.

questions.question: What type of user (persona) has clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform and have one or more roles (i.e. itil and approver_user)?
questions.explanation: Process User is the persona with clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform, holding roles like itil and approver_user. Process Users follow structured ITSM processes (Incident, Problem, Change management). Approving Managers handle approvals; Service Desk Users handle front-line tickets; ITSM User and Workflow User are not standard ServiceNow persona names.

questions.question: You are asked to create an option for users to click Get Help and describe an issue, creating incident records automatically routed to the Service Desk. Which method would you use?
questions.explanation: A Record Producer is the best method for creating a 'Get Help' option that generates incident records. Record Producers are Service Catalog items that create records on a specified table (like Incident) when submitted. Users fill out a simple form describing their issue, and the resulting incident is automatically routed to the Service Desk via assignment rules or workflows. Catalog Items and Order Guides serve different ordering purposes.

questions.question: What is the name of the table relationship where two or more tables are related in a bi-directional relationship, so that related records are visible from both tables in a related list?
questions.explanation: A Many-to-Many relationship links two tables where records in each table can relate to multiple records in the other table. For example, a user can belong to many groups, and a group can have many users. This is implemented via a relationship table (M2M table) that stores pairs of references. One-to-Many means one parent has multiple children; One-to-One means a direct 1:1 link.

questions.question: What feature do you use to specify which users are able to access a Service Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is used to specify which users can access a Service Catalog Item. User Criteria evaluates conditions like roles, groups, departments, companies, or locations to determine who can view and order catalog items. ACLs control table/field-level security but are not the mechanism for catalog item visibility. The 'Available for' tab on catalog items uses User Criteria.

questions.question: Table Access Control rules are processed in the following order:
options: any table name (wildcard), parent table name, table name
table name, parent table name, any table name (wildcard)
any table name (wildcard), table name, parent table name
parent table name, table name, any table name (wildcard)
questions.explanation: Table ACL rules are processed in order of specificity: table name first, then parent table name, then wildcard (*). ServiceNow checks the most specific ACL (exact table match) first. If no match, it checks the parent table's ACLs. Finally, it checks the wildcard (*) rule that applies to all tables. This ensures specific rules take priority over general ones.

questions.question: What types of entities can receive task assignments in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow, task assignments can be made to Users and Groups. The Assigned to field references a user, and the Assignment group field references a group. Teams and Departments are organizational concepts but are not direct assignment targets on task records.

questions.question: You have been asked to create a way for users to order a new iPhone, but only if they get two levels of approval. What feature would you use to manage the approvals and notifications?
questions.explanation: Flows in Flow Designer provide a visual, no-code way to automate multi-step processes including approvals, notifications, and record updates. For creating a way for users to order an iPhone with conditions, Flow Designer with a catalog item is the best approach. Approval Policies set approval rules but don't build the full ordering workflow.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow capability allows you to provide knowledge articles via a conversational messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is the ServiceNow capability that provides knowledge articles via a conversational messaging interface. It uses Natural Language Understanding (NLU) to interpret user queries and surfaces relevant KB articles in a chat format. Agent Assist helps fulfillers but isn't a user-facing chatbot; Now Messenger is not a standard ServiceNow product.

questions.question: Access Control rules may provide access security for which of the following database objects?
options: For a specific role, group, or user
For a specific row, column, or table
For a specific CMDB Configuration item
questions.explanation: Access Control List (ACL) rules provide security for a specific row, column, or table. ACLs can be defined at the table level (controlling access to all records), field/column level (controlling access to specific fields), and row level (using conditions to restrict specific records). They don't directly govern role or group definitions.

questions.question: A new Service Desk employee complains that the create dates and times are incorrect on their Incident list. What would you suggest to fix this issue?
options: Have them correct the time zone on their computer
Have them use the gear icon to set the employee's time zone
Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer
Use the system properties to correct the instance's time zone
questions.explanation: The issue is likely a time zone mismatch. The fix is to have the employee use the gear icon in their profile to set the correct time zone. ServiceNow displays dates/times based on the user's configured time zone, not the browser or OS setting. If the user's ServiceNow time zone doesn't match their actual location, dates will appear incorrect.

questions.question: On a filter condition, there is an element which is based on the table, the user access rights, and columns on the table. What is this element called?
questions.explanation: On a filter condition, the Field element is based on the table, user access rights, and is dynamically populated. It determines which fields are available for filtering.

questions.question: A customer has asked for updates to a form: Make Resolution code Mandatory when state is Resolved; Hide Major Incident checkbox unless user has Major Incident Manager role. What type of rule would you use?
questions.explanation: To make fields mandatory, read-only, or hidden based on conditions (like making Resolution Notes mandatory when State = Resolved), you should use a UI Policy. UI Policies provide a no-code way to dynamically change field behavior on forms. Business Rules run server-side and are better for data logic; Dictionary settings are static and can't respond to field changes.

questions.question: Which mobile application is designed to interact with customer support and is not customizable?
questions.explanation: Now Support (formerly HI Support) is the mobile app for interacting with customer support. It's not customizable, unlike Now Mobile which can be configured.

questions.question: The customer has asked that you change the default layout of the Task list with specific columns in a specific order. How would you do this?
options: Right click on any column header, Context Menu > Configure > List Layout
Click List Context Menu > Configure > Columns
Click List Context Menu > Personalize List
Right click List Gear icon > Configure > Columns
questions.explanation: To change the default list layout for all users, right-click on any column header and use the Context Menu > Configure > List Layout. This is an admin-level change.

questions.question: What is the most common role that has access to almost all platform features, functions, and data?
questions.explanation: The System Administrator [admin] role has access to almost all platform features. It's the most powerful OOTB role in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Automated Chatting agent available on the service portal is commonly referred to as?
questions.explanation: The Virtual Agent is ServiceNow's AI-powered chatbot available on the Service Portal. It handles common requests, provides answers, and can create tickets.

questions.question: You cannot deactivate a plugin, once it has been activated.
questions.explanation: Once activated, plugins cannot be deactivated. This is true — you should carefully evaluate plugins before activation as the change is permanent.

questions.question: Where can Admins check which release is running on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: Admins can check the running release via the Stats module (type 'stats.do' in the navigator). It shows build info, version, node details, and instance stats.

questions.question: Which testing framework is used to test ServiceNow Applications?
questions.explanation: The Automated Test Framework (ATF) is ServiceNow's built-in testing tool. It creates and runs automated tests for forms, flows, scripts, and other platform features.

questions.question: Which module is used to access the knowledge bases available to a particular non-admin user?
questions.explanation: Non-admin users access knowledge bases through Self-Service > Knowledge. This module shows only the knowledge bases the user has permission to view.

questions.question: What is a no-code approach to control the mandatory or read-only state of a form field?
questions.explanation: UI Policy is the no-code approach to control mandatory, read-only, and visible states of form fields. Unlike Client Scripts, UI Policies don't require scripting.

questions.question: What type of query allows you to filter list data using normal words, instead of the condition builder?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Query (NLQ) allows users to filter lists using plain English phrases instead of building conditions manually. It interprets words and converts them to filters.

questions.question: When managing tags, what are the visibility options?
questions.explanation: Tag visibility options are: Everyone (all users can see), Me (only the creator), and Groups and Users (specific people). Roles/permissions and Admin are not tag visibility options.

questions.question: How would you distinguish between a Base Class table and a Parent Class table?
options: Extended tables can be extended from Parent tables or Base tables; but not both
Base Class tables always have tables extended from them. Parent tables do not.
Extended tables are always extended from Parent tables. Extended tables are usually extended from Base tables.
Base Class table is not extended from another table. Parent class tables may be extended from another table.
questions.explanation: A Base Class table is one that is not extended from another table but may have tables extending from it. A Parent Class table has child extensions.

questions.question: How are products and services in the Service Catalog organized?
questions.explanation: Service Catalog items are organized into Categories and Subcategories. Categories group related items together, making it easy for users to browse and find services.

questions.question: A record is added to which table each time a knowledge article is viewed?
questions.explanation: Each time a knowledge article is viewed, a record is added to the Knowledge Use [kb_use] table. This tracks article views, helping identify popular and useful content.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to categorize, flag, and locate records?
questions.explanation: Tags are used to categorize, flag, and locate records in ServiceNow. They provide a flexible way to organize records beyond standard fields and categories.

questions.question: Banner Color can be personalized from which section in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Banner Color can be personalized from the Themes section in ServiceNow. Themes control the overall look including colors, fonts, and branding.

questions.question: What defines and monitors the guarantees established with an outside supplier?
questions.explanation: An Underpinning Contract (UC) defines and monitors guarantees with external suppliers. It's the supplier-facing equivalent of an SLA.

questions.question: After high security plugin is activated, a security_admin privilege is created. What is an elevated privilege?
options: Used to enable the ITIL role to have an Admin type access
Elevated privilege is used to promote extension tables
A role that has special permissions for the duration of the log in session
questions.explanation: An elevated privilege is a role with special permissions for the duration of a session. After activating high security plugin, security_admin becomes an elevated privilege that must be explicitly activated per session.

questions.question: Out of the below listed applications, which will NOT run natively on smartphones?
questions.explanation: Workflow is a back-office automation tool that does NOT run natively on smartphones. Service Catalog, Self-Service, and User Administration all have mobile-friendly interfaces.

questions.question: When is a workflow complete?
options: When the workflow runs out of activities
When the workflow reached to Delivery stage
When the workflow reached to End Activity
When the workflow reached to Complete stage
questions.explanation: A workflow is complete when it reaches the End Activity. Every workflow must have exactly one Begin and one End activity. The End activity marks the successful completion of the workflow.

questions.question: How does ServiceNow decide which application should be visible when a user logs in?
options: Everybody can see all the applications
Defined on the basis of roles assigned to the user
questions.explanation: ServiceNow determines visible applications based on roles assigned to the user. Each application and module has role requirements — users only see what their roles permit.

questions.question: Which of the following options is an example of a UI Policy?
options: Creating a new field on form
questions.explanation: Making the priority field mandatory is a classic example of a UI Policy. UI Policies control field states (mandatory, read-only, visible) based on conditions without scripting.

questions.question: How do you monitor your ServiceNow servlet?
questions.explanation: You monitor the ServiceNow servlet health by navigating to stats.do. It displays servlet status, memory usage, active transactions, and node information.

questions.question: Where can Pause condition be used in SLA?
options: It can be put on any desired field
questions.explanation: Pause conditions in SLA can be used on any desired field. While commonly used for Pending/Hold states, the pause condition is flexible and can reference any field.

questions.question: Which one of the following contains text search options?
questions.explanation: All of the above — text search is available in Knowledge (article search), Homepages (widget search), and Lists (column text search). ServiceNow provides search across multiple interfaces.

questions.question: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report outage: what do these services in the Service Catalog have in common?
options: They direct the user to a catalog property
They direct the user to a record producer
They direct the user to a catalog UI policy
They direct the user to a catalog client script
questions.explanation: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report Outage are examples of Record Producers. Record producers allow end users to create records in backend tables through the Service Catalog.

questions.question: The manager plans to send the same report every month to the client via email. What can help with this?
options: Date/Time field on the report record
questions.explanation: A Scheduled Report allows you to automatically generate and email reports on a recurring basis — daily, weekly, monthly, etc.

questions.question: What do you need to do before you can use an Application-based trigger in your flow?
options: Assign Application trigger role [sn_app_trigger_write] to SME
Activate application spoke, and plug-ins as needed
questions.explanation: Before using application-based triggers in Flow Designer, you need to activate the application spoke and required plug-ins. Spokes contain the triggers and actions for specific applications.

questions.question: What is a key difference between Reporting and Performance Analytics?
options: Reports can be run on a scheduled basis; Performance Analytics cannot.
Performance Analytics can show trends; Reports cannot.
Performance Analytics contains snapshots of data taken over time; Reporting shows only the data as it is at the moment the report is run.
Performance Analytics data can be published to Dashboards; Reports cannot.
Performance Analytics shows KPIs; Reporting does not.
questions.explanation: The key difference is that Performance Analytics contains snapshots of data taken over time, enabling trend analysis. Standard reports show current-state data only.

questions.question: The ServiceNow platform includes which types of interfaces? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow platform includes Now Mobile Apps, Service Portals, and Now Platform User Interfaces (Next Experience, UI16). Back Office Dashboard and Agent Control Center are not standard interface types.

questions.question: Which database provides a logical model of your company infrastructure by identifying, controlling, maintaining and verifying CIs?
questions.explanation: The CMDB (Configuration Management Database) provides a logical model of IT infrastructure by identifying, controlling, and verifying configuration items and their relationships.

questions.question: There is no need to create new Import Set for every time you need to import data, you can reuse the Import Set if importing data with the same columns.
questions.explanation: True — you can reuse existing Import Sets for recurring imports. There's no need to create a new one each time; you can re-run the same import set with updated data.

questions.question: What ServiceNow API will you use to retrieve the incident data in the server script?
questions.explanation: GlideRecord is the server-side API for querying and manipulating records. g_form is client-side only, and GlideApi/GlideData don't exist in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Which of the following modules can be used to track the requests that you submitted?
questions.explanation: To track your submitted requests, use Self-Service > My Requests. This shows all service catalog requests you've submitted along with their status.

questions.question: Delegated developers automatically get the permission for deployment.
questions.explanation: False — delegated developers do NOT automatically get deployment permissions. Deployment rights must be explicitly granted by an admin.

questions.question: You can approve/reject an approval request record by right clicking the approval request in the list and selecting approve or reject.
questions.explanation: True — you can right-click an approval request in a list to quickly approve or reject it. This provides a shortcut without opening the full record.

questions.question: Import Articles button can be used to import articles from Word documents into the knowledge base.
questions.explanation: True — the Import Articles button allows bulk importing of Word documents (.docx) into knowledge bases, converting them to knowledge articles.

questions.question: Related lists do NOT appear on a form until a record has been saved to the database.
questions.explanation: True — related lists only appear after a record has been saved because they depend on the record's sys_id to establish relationships with other tables.

questions.question: ATF can consist of steps that run on web browser.
questions.explanation: True — ATF (Automated Test Framework) can include steps that simulate browser interactions like clicking buttons, filling forms, and navigating pages.

questions.question: Which module displays a list of tasks assigned to a user's group but not yet to a specific user?
questions.explanation: The Service Desk > My Groups Work module shows tasks assigned to your group but not yet assigned to a specific individual. These are unassigned group tasks.

questions.question: Which module can be used to see a list of events that have been triggered?
questions.explanation: To see a list of events that have been generated, navigate to System Policy > Events > Event Log. The Event Log records all events fired in the instance, including who triggered them and when. This is useful for debugging notification issues and verifying that Business Rules or workflows are generating expected events.

questions.question: The problem_task table extends which table?
options: There is no table such as problem_task
It does not extend any table
questions.explanation: The problem_task table extends the Task [task] table. In ServiceNow, most work-related tables — including incident, change_request, problem, and problem_task — extend the base Task table, inheriting common fields like state, assignment group, priority, and work notes.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a type of Visual Task Board?
questions.explanation: The Visual Task Board types are: Freeform (flexible layout without lane constraints), Guided (lanes based on field values like State), and Flexible (customizable lanes). Feature is NOT a type of Visual Task Board — it's a concept in Agile Development, not a VTB type.

questions.question: A group can contain a nested group.
questions.explanation: True. A group in ServiceNow can contain nested (child) groups. This creates a hierarchy where a parent group includes all members of its child groups. For example, an 'IT Support' group could contain 'Network Support' and 'Desktop Support' as nested groups. This is useful for cascading assignments and approvals up the management chain.

questions.question: What records can be created when placing an order in the Service Catalog? Select 3 answers
questions.explanation: When placing an order in the Service Catalog, three types of records are created: a Request [sc_request] representing the overall order, one or more Requested Items [sc_req_item] for each catalog item ordered, and Catalog Tasks [sc_task] for the fulfillment steps assigned to teams. Problem Tasks and Change Requests are not part of the Service Catalog ordering process.

questions.question: How is it possible for a non-administrator to develop and deploy applications on the Now Platform?
options: Ask the administrators to do it since only administrators have this level of access.
It is not possible to develop or deploy applications in ServiceNow.
It is not necessary for a non-administrator to develop or deploy applications.
Use delegated development and deployment application.
questions.explanation: A non-administrator can develop and deploy applications using Delegated Development. Administrators grant specific users the right to develop within designated application scopes. This allows developers to create and modify applications without needing the full admin role, maintaining security while enabling development agility.

questions.question: Who can access schema maps, tables and column module?
questions.explanation: Only Administrators can access Schema Maps, Tables, and the Columns module. These are system definition tools under System Definition that allow viewing and modifying the database structure. ITIL users and end users don't have the admin role required to view or modify table schemas and column definitions.

questions.question: When you have subject filled on email notification as well as on the notification template, which one will appear on the sent email?
questions.explanation: When both an Email Notification and its Notification Template have a subject line defined, the subject from the Email Notification takes precedence. The template provides defaults, but the notification record's fields override the template values. This allows you to reuse templates while customizing individual notifications.

questions.question: Which of the following is possible via an inbound action?
questions.explanation: An Inbound Email Action can create new records, update existing records, or run scripts based on incoming emails. For example, an email to the incident inbox can create a new incident, or a reply to an existing notification can add comments to the record. Inbound actions match emails using conditions and process them with defined actions.

questions.question: What is a ServiceNow event?
options: Business rules, client scripts, fields, forms and form sections, reports, tables, views and workflows
Create a new table and fill out the extend table field
It is an indication to the ServiceNow processes that something notable has occurred, e.g., approving a request, workflow, etc.
Semaphores, which control the number of user transactions that can be run in parallel.
questions.explanation: A ServiceNow Event is a system-generated signal that something notable occurred — such as a record insert, a state change, or a threshold breach. Events are logged in the Event Log and can trigger Notifications, Script Actions, or other responses. They decouple the 'what happened' from the 'what to do about it', enabling flexible automation.

questions.question: When can SLA actions be triggered on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: SLA actions can be triggered anytime — not just when an SLA is breached, completed, or in progress. SLA actions (such as notifications, escalations, or script executions) can be configured to run at any stage of the SLA lifecycle: when the SLA attaches, while it's in progress, when it's paused, when it breaches, or when it completes. The answer 'Anytime' reflects that SLA actions are not limited to a single phase.

questions.question: What's a module and application in the example: Incident > Create New
options: Incident is an application and Create New is the module
Incident is a module and Create New is an application
Incident and Create New both are applications
Incident and Create New both are modules
questions.explanation: In the example 'Incident > Create New', Incident is the Application and Create New is the Module. Applications are top-level groupings in the Application Navigator (left sidebar), and modules are the clickable links within each application that navigate to lists, forms, or other content.

questions.question: Which of the following concepts are associated with the ServiceNow CMDB?
questions.explanation: The CMDB is associated with: Configuration Items (CIs) — the assets/components tracked; CI Classes — the categorization hierarchy; CI Relationships — dependencies between CIs; and Discovery — automated population of CI data. Baselines, Health Dashboard, and Identification Rules are also core CMDB concepts.

questions.question: What details does a knowledge article hold?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, B, C: Known errors and User Solutions and Troubleshooting tips. Options like "User information" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Is it true that System upgrade schedule auto-updates an existing MID server to the latest build on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: False. The System Upgrade Schedule does NOT auto-update existing MID Servers. MID Servers must be manually upgraded or configured for auto-upgrade separately. The System Upgrade Schedule pertains to instance upgrades (platform version updates), not MID Server updates. Administrators need to manage MID Server upgrades through the MID Server management console.

questions.question: Resetting the list layout globally will graphically reset the preferences of all users for that table.
questions.explanation: True. Resetting the list layout globally will reset the column preferences for ALL users viewing that list. This reverts the list to the system default layout, removing any personalized column selections users have made. Individual users can re-personalize their view afterward. This is why global list layout changes should be communicated to users.

questions.question: Form Context Menu provides a graphical representation of other tables related to a specific table.
questions.explanation: False. The Form Context Menu (accessed by right-clicking a field label) provides options like Configure Dictionary, Configure Label, Show/Hide field, and other field-level actions. It does NOT provide a graphical representation of related tables. The Schema Map is the feature that shows a visual diagram of table relationships.

questions.question: When relating to Task SLA Time-Based Fields, The Breach time is the same as Planned end time.
questions.explanation: False. In Task SLA records, Planned end time is the calculated date/time when the SLA is scheduled to breach, while Breach time is set only when the SLA actually breaches. They can differ — for example, if the SLA was paused and resumed, or if schedules/conditions changed before breach occurred.

questions.question: Which is the correct role that allows personalising a list view on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The personalize_list role allows users to personalize their own list views on a ServiceNow instance. With this role, users can add/remove columns, change column order, and save their preferred list layout. Without it, users see only the default admin-configured list layout. The personalize role covers forms, while personalize_list is specifically for list views.

questions.question: What is retroactive start in SLA?
options: It is used for attaching SLA from a particularly created date & time without attaching SLA on the opened time.
This is used for calculating duration of SLA.
Through this field we can stop SLA on any condition.
This field is not there on SLA Definition page.
questions.explanation: Retroactive Start in SLA allows an SLA to begin counting from a point in the past rather than when the SLA was attached. For example, if an SLA definition is added after an incident is created, retroactive start can calculate the SLA from the incident's creation time rather than the current time. This ensures accurate time tracking even when SLA definitions are applied after the fact.

questions.question: Can you change the number prefix from "INC" to "IN" for incident table?
questions.explanation: Yes, you can change the number prefix by going to System Definition > Number Maintenance (sys_number table). Each table with auto-numbering has an entry here where you can modify the prefix (e.g., 'INC' to 'IN'), number of digits, and current counter. Changes only affect new records — existing records keep their original numbers.

questions.question: What enhanced notification preferences options are available for users?
options: Set global notification preferences for all active users in the system.
Enable or disable a particular channel for receiving notifications.
Create, edit, or delete notification channels for instant messages, email, SMS, and voice.
Create, edit, or delete system notifications for a particular channel.
Create custom notifications by subscribing to system notifications and applying desired conditions.
questions.explanation: Enhanced notification preferences allow users to: Enable or disable a particular channel (email, SMS, push) for receiving notifications; Set digest intervals to batch notifications instead of receiving them individually; and Subscribe/unsubscribe from specific notifications marked as subscribable. These give end users control over how they receive alerts.

questions.question: What can you do with a service catalog item once it's built?
options: Publish it in the service catalog
questions.explanation: Once a service catalog item is built, you can do all of the above — publish it to make it available for ordering, test it to verify the workflow and approvals work correctly, and configure additional settings like variables, pricing, and fulfillment rules. Service catalog items go through a build-test-publish lifecycle.

questions.question: What do requesters see when they go to the service catalog?
questions.explanation: When requesters go to the Service Catalog, they see self-service items — catalog items and record producers that they are authorized to request. The catalog displays items organized by categories, with descriptions, icons, and pricing. Requesters don't see backend configurations, fulfillment workflows, or admin settings.

questions.question: Where do you change the banner of the application?
options: System Properties and in CSS Properties
questions.explanation: To change the banner of the application, go to System Properties and CSS Properties. System Properties (System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16) controls the banner image and text. CSS Properties allow further customization of colors, fonts, and layout of the banner area. Both work together for complete banner customization.

questions.question: If the Default update set is marked complete:
options: The changes are tracked in the user's current update set.
The system creates another update set named Default1 and uses it as the default update set.
The default update set cannot be marked completed.
questions.explanation: If the Default update set is marked complete, the system automatically creates a new update set named 'Default1' and sets it as the current update set. ServiceNow always needs an active default update set to capture configuration changes. The default update set cannot remain in a completed state — the system ensures there's always one available.

questions.question: Which of the following modules are available to ITIL users by default?
questions.explanation: ITIL users by default have access to: Incident, Problem, Change, and Service Catalog modules. These are the core ITSM applications that fulfiller users need. The ITIL role grants read/write access to task-based tables. CMDB is accessible but primarily managed by cmdb_read/cmdb roles. HR and Security Operations require separate roles.

questions.question: A new group has been created to access service catalog requests however the group members are not able to access it. What is the BEST practice?
options: Assign catalog role to the group and then add users to the group
Assign catalog role to individual users and then add them to the group
Assign catalog role to individual users
Assign catalog role to individual users and to the group
questions.explanation: The group members likely need the catalog role or need to be added to the correct assignment group for service catalog fulfillment. Without proper roles, group members can't see or fulfill catalog requests even if the group is correctly created. Check that users have the itil role and that the catalog item's fulfillment group matches the new group.

questions.question: How do you get to the categories on an incident and other table?
options: Go to System Definition > Choice List
Go to Social IT > Feed Administration > Messages
questions.explanation: To access categories (choice values) for fields on the Incident or other tables, go to System Definition > Choice List. This module shows all choice values across all tables. You can filter by table name and field name to find specific categories like incident Priority, State, or Category values. You can also right-click a field and select 'Show Choice List'.

questions.question: All workflows absolutely must have a beginning and an end.
questions.explanation: True. All workflows in ServiceNow must have a Begin activity and an End activity. The Begin activity is the entry point (triggered by a condition or event), and the End activity marks completion. Without both, the workflow cannot execute properly. Workflows can have multiple End activities for different paths but only one Begin.

questions.question: Which among the following tables cannot be deleted?
options: Semaphores that control the number of user transactions
Approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers, utilities
To automate a sequence of activities
questions.explanation: A Base Table (like Task or cmdb_ci) cannot be deleted because many other tables extend from it and core platform functionality depends on it. Deleting a base table would break all child tables and associated business logic. Custom tables and standalone tables can be deleted if they have no dependencies. System tables are also protected from deletion.

questions.question: What is the search engine used while doing the global search in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow uses the Zing search engine for global text search. It indexes records across tables and provides fast, full-text search results.

questions.question: Where would you create the order guide choices/questions?
options: Go to the order guide and go to the variables section
Go to Social IT > Feed Administration
questions.explanation: Order guide choices/questions are created by going to the order guide record and adding variables in the variables section. Variables define the questions users answer when ordering.

questions.question: How to capture a workflow in update sets?
questions.explanation: To capture a workflow in an update set, you must Publish the workflow. Only published workflows are tracked in the current update set.

questions.question: What is an access control?
options: It is a security rule defined and set at the row level and the column level, and it is executed when attempting to access any ServiceNow table
It is a security rule defined and set on field level, and it is executed when attempting to access any ServiceNow record
Access control is a role provided out of the box in ServiceNow
questions.explanation: An Access Control (ACL) is a security rule defined at the row level. It determines who can access specific records based on roles, conditions, and scripts.

questions.question: Inbound action can be used to:
questions.explanation: Inbound email actions can parse emails, modify existing records, and create new records. They cannot schedule jobs — that's done through Scheduled Jobs module.

questions.question: What is a data policy?
options: Enables admins to set mandatory and read-only states for fields and can enforce data consistency across applications.
It's the control record of the table and determines whether the table will be audited, default sorting, attributes of table.
It's a series of tables that contain all the assets and business services controlled by your company.
questions.explanation: A Data Policy enables admins to set mandatory and read-only states on fields that are enforced across all data entry channels — forms, imports, web services, and APIs.

questions.question: What is a UI policy?
options: Its a required field that requires a value
It's a rule that applies to a form to dynamically change the ways the fields behave in a form
It's a script that applies to a form to dynamically change form information or the form itself
questions.explanation: A UI Policy is a rule that dynamically changes form behavior — making fields mandatory, read-only, or visible/hidden based on conditions. It applies only to the form interface.

questions.question: Where would you go to start an import set?
questions.explanation: To start an import set, navigate to System Import Sets > Load Data. This module lets you upload files or connect to data sources to begin the import process.

questions.question: What gets skipped during a major upgrade?
options: Read only data of a form that is not editable
All system features, applications, functions, and data
Any record that has been altered from the base state. The upgrade app looks at the customer update table (e.g., sys_update_xml)
questions.explanation: During a major upgrade, any record that has been altered from the base state (customized) is skipped to preserve your customizations. Unmodified records get updated.

questions.question: Which of the following can be an example of an Out Of The Box table?
questions.explanation: The incident table is an OOTB (Out of the Box) table. Tables prefixed with 'u_' are custom global tables, and 'x_' prefixed tables belong to scoped applications.

questions.question: Which among the following is true regarding UI Policies?
options: They run only on server side
All the UI Policies of task table are not extended by the incident table
Based on the condition, it can be decided when to make it visible/hidden
They run on the cloud side
questions.explanation: UI Policies evaluate conditions to determine when to apply field changes. The condition controls when the policy triggers — making fields mandatory, read-only, or hidden dynamically.

questions.question: ACLs can be defined in how many ways?
questions.explanation: ACLs can be defined using all of the above: Conditional Expressions (field-based conditions), Scripts (advanced logic), and Roles (role-based access). These can be combined.

questions.question: Like business rules, notifications can be created when a record is inserted or updated.
questions.explanation: True — like business rules, notifications can be configured to trigger on record insert, update, or both. They use similar 'When' conditions to determine firing.

questions.question: What is SLM?
questions.explanation: SLM stands for Service Level Management. It's the ITIL practice of defining, monitoring, and reporting on service level agreements between IT and business.

questions.question: Where would you go to create an order guide?
options: Service catalog > catalog definition > order guides and click new
Go to system definition > choice list
questions.explanation: Order guides are created at Service Catalog > Catalog Definition > Order Guides. This is the standard module for managing order guide records.

questions.question: Multiple Choice, Single Text, and Select Box are what type of elements in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Multiple Choice, Single Text, and Select Box are Variable Types in ServiceNow. Variables are form elements on catalog items that capture user input.

questions.question: An ACL is __ type of security.
questions.explanation: An ACL is contextual security — it evaluates access based on the context of who is accessing what record, under what conditions, and with which roles.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the steps of a Knowledge article?
questions.explanation: The correct knowledge article lifecycle is: Draft → Review → Publish → Retire. Articles start as drafts, go through SME review, get published, and are eventually retired.

questions.question: The upgrade history module helps an admin locate and resolve upgrade conflicts.
questions.explanation: True — the Upgrade History module helps administrators find and resolve upgrade conflicts. It lists all upgrades and highlights any skipped or conflicting files.

questions.question: What are update sets?
options: Customization that can be moved from 1 instance to another
questions.explanation: Update sets are customizations that can be moved from one instance to another. They capture configuration changes (not data) and enable controlled deployment across environments.

questions.question: In service catalog application, which module is used for creating items?
questions.explanation: The Maintain Items module in Service Catalog is used for creating and managing catalog items. It provides the full catalog item form with all configuration options.

questions.question: All users can manage and setup import sets.
questions.explanation: False — only users with the admin or import_admin role can manage and set up import sets. Regular users don't have import permissions.

questions.question: A Business rule can be set before or after the database action has occurred.
questions.explanation: True — business rules can be configured to run before the database operation (to validate/modify data) or after (to trigger follow-up actions).

questions.question: Types of SLA (SLA, OLA & UC) are defined in which field?
questions.explanation: SLA types (SLA, OLA, UC) are defined in the Type field on the SLA Definition record. This field distinguishes between customer-facing SLAs, internal OLAs, and supplier UCs.

questions.question: What are the out of box progress stages for a Service Request?
questions.explanation: The OOTB progress stages for a Service Request include all of the above: Waiting for Approval, Fulfillment, and Delivery. These represent the standard request lifecycle.

questions.question: What is true about deleting tables?
options: An ESS user can delete any table
Deleting a table does not delete associated elements like views
Only tables beginning with "u_" can be permanently deleted
questions.explanation: Only tables beginning with 'u_' (custom tables) can be permanently deleted. OOTB/core tables cannot be deleted to protect system integrity.

questions.question: What are the main tools you can use to automate ServiceNow?
options: UI policy, data policies, UI actions and scripts
Lists, global text search, navigation filter, live feed
questions.explanation: The main automation tools are UI Policies, Data Policies, UI Actions, and Scripts (Business Rules, Client Scripts, Script Includes). These form the core automation toolkit.

questions.question: Which one is used to group related fields together?
questions.explanation: Sections are used to group related fields together on a form. They create visual divisions with headers, making long forms more organized and readable.

questions.question: What database kept all the customization that you made on your instance?
questions.explanation: All customizations are stored in the sys_update_xml table. Each customization record contains the XML representation of the change, linked to its update set.

questions.question: What does a dictionary override do?
options: It updates the db fields and brings you back to a list
Set fields on a form from to visible or hidden; editable or read only; optional or mandatory
It provides the ability to override several aspects of a field in extended tables
questions.explanation: A Dictionary Override allows you to change field properties (like default value, mandatory, read-only) on an extended table without affecting the parent table's definition.

questions.question: To create two columns in a form, how many splits should be used?
questions.explanation: To create two columns in a form, you need one split. A single split divides the form into two columns. Two splits would create three columns.

questions.question: What does a patch release fix?
options: It allows you to update the record without having to go into a form
Combines hot fixes from last feature release and does other fixes
Define the questions to ask from the end user ordering the catalog item
questions.explanation: A patch release combines hot fixes from the last feature release and delivers critical bug fixes and security updates between major releases.

questions.question: What is a healthy total response time for Network, browser & server?
questions.explanation: A healthy total response time for ServiceNow is 3 seconds on average across network, browser, and server. Anything above this indicates performance issues.

questions.question: What does SAAS stand for?
questions.explanation: SaaS stands for Software as a Service. ServiceNow is a SaaS platform — the software is hosted in the cloud and accessed via web browser.

questions.question: Which of the following is most suitable to apply governance rules to decide who can access certain fields in certain tables?
questions.explanation: ACLs (Access Control Lists) are the most suitable for governance rules controlling who can access what data. UI Policies and Client Scripts handle form behavior, not security.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes Predictive Intelligence?
options: Predictive Intelligence uses predefined configurations to set field values
Predictive Intelligence uses machine learning algorithms to set the "assignment group" and the "assigned to" fields
Predictive Intelligence uses machine learning algorithms to set field values during record creation
Predictive Intelligence uses assignment rules to set the "Assigned to" field
questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence uses machine learning algorithms to make predictions about records — auto-categorizing, auto-prioritizing, and auto-assigning incidents based on historical patterns.

questions.question: You need to create a new field in a table. What field type should you use if your field needs to display records from another table?
questions.explanation: Use a Reference field type when a field needs to retrieve and reference records from another table. Reference fields create relationships between tables.

questions.question: Every task can be assigned to an assignment group and to a specific user at the same time.
questions.explanation: True — a task can be simultaneously assigned to an assignment group AND a specific user within that group. Both fields can have values at the same time.

questions.question: Which prefix is used for custom tables in the global application?
questions.explanation: Custom tables in the global application scope use the 'u_' prefix. Scoped application tables use 'x_[vendor]_[app]_' prefix.

questions.question: Which of the following chart types can be created directly by right-clicking a list?
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a list lets you create Bar charts and Pie charts directly. Other chart types (Line, Area, Donut, Bubble) require the full Report Designer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a set of tables containing assets and business services controlled by a company?
questions.explanation: The CMDB is the set of tables containing assets and business services controlled by IT. It's the central repository for all configuration item data.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is used to store data in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Tables store data in ServiceNow. Forms display/edit individual records, Lists show multiple records, but the underlying storage mechanism is always tables.

questions.question: Which of the following contains Flow Designer triggers and actions dedicated to a particular application?
questions.explanation: A Spoke contains Flow Designer triggers and actions dedicated to a particular application or service (e.g., Slack Spoke, Teams Spoke, ITSM Spoke).

questions.question: The Activity Stream is an example of a formatter.
questions.explanation: True — the Activity Stream is a formatter. Formatters are special form elements that display non-field content like activity streams, process flows, or approval summaries.

questions.question: Data policies can be applied to a table and can be enforced on both the form and the list.
questions.explanation: True — Data Policies can enforce mandatory and read-only rules on both forms and lists. They work across all data input channels.

questions.question: The purpose of data policies is to enforce security in the system.
questions.explanation: False — Data Policies enforce data consistency, not security. ACLs handle security. Data Policies ensure fields have valid values regardless of input channel.

questions.question: One of the disadvantages of assignment rules is that they can only use configurations but no scripting can be added.
questions.explanation: False — assignment rules CAN use scripts in addition to conditions. The scripting option allows complex logic for determining assignments.

questions.question: Which one of the following authentication methods is not supported in ServiceNow?
options: All the listed methods are supported in ServiceNow
questions.explanation: All the listed methods are supported in ServiceNow: OAuth, SAML, LDAP, and Digest Token are all valid authentication methods. ServiceNow supports a wide range of auth protocols.

questions.question: The Analytics Center provides the Platform Analytics Workspace with a single page for all the dashboards, visualizations, analytics answers, and insights on your instance.
