questions.explanation: The Analytics Center provides a single-page workspace for all analytics needs. It consolidates Performance Analytics, reporting, and dashboards into one unified interface.

questions.question: Which one of the following orders is used by default to sort lists?
questions.explanation: By default, ServiceNow sorts lists using the order: Order → Number → Name. The Order field (if present) is checked first, then Number, and finally Name as the tiebreaker. This default sort order applies to most list views unless a custom sort has been configured.

questions.question: Which of the following context menus can be used to configure the list?
questions.explanation: The Column Context Menu (right-click on a column header in a list) provides options to configure the list, including: Sort ascending/descending, Group by this column, Configure List Layout, Create Quick Report, Show Visual Task Board, and Export. The Record Context Menu and Title Bar Menu serve different purposes — record-level and list-level actions respectively.

questions.question: How can you filter the types of activities that are displayed in the Activity section?
options: Navigate to Service Desk > Personalization and update the record
It is not possible to filter the activity types in the Activity section
Navigate to Service Desk > Personalization and add a record
Click on the gear icon in the top banner and select which activity types
Click on the funnel icon in the task form and select which activity types to show
questions.explanation: You can filter activities displayed in the Activity section by clicking the filter icon at the top of the Activity stream. This lets you select which activity types to show — such as Comments, Work Notes, Emails, Field Changes, or System activities. This filtering is per-user and per-form, helping fulfillers focus on relevant updates without noise.

questions.question: What is the limit of Templates that can be made for a form?
questions.explanation: There is no hard limit on the number of templates that can be created for a form in ServiceNow. Users can create as many templates as needed. Templates save pre-filled field values that can be applied when creating new records, speeding up data entry. Templates can be personal (visible only to the creator) or shared (visible to groups/roles).

questions.question: Every list can have only one view.
questions.explanation: False. A list in ServiceNow can have multiple views. Administrators can create different list views to show different columns and layouts for the same table. Users can switch between views using the list context menu, and specific views can be assigned to different roles.

questions.question: You need to move your work from development instance to production instance. What can you use?
questions.explanation: Update Sets are used to move customizations from a development instance to production. They capture changes to configuration records (Business Rules, UI Policies, form layouts, etc.) and package them for transfer. Changes are exported as XML from the source instance and imported into the target. This ensures controlled migration without manual re-creation of changes.

questions.question: You are designing a form for a specific record. Which of the following is useful when you want to show records in the tables that have relationships to the current record?
questions.explanation: A Related List displays records from other tables that have a relationship to the current record. For example, on an Incident form, related lists can show child tasks, approvals, or work notes. Related lists appear at the bottom of the form and are configured through the form designer or by personalizing the form layout.

questions.question: You are designing a record producer. You need to add questions to the form to solicit information from customers. Which of the following should you use?
questions.explanation: Variables are form fields on Service Catalog items that capture user input during the ordering process. They're like custom fields specific to a catalog item — examples include text fields, dropdowns, checkboxes, and reference fields. Variables differ from table fields in that they're stored in the sc_item_option_mtom table, not on the target table directly.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to display a set of records?
questions.explanation: A List is used to display a set of records from a table in ServiceNow. Lists show multiple records in a tabular format with columns for each field. A Form displays a single record, a Table is the underlying data structure, and a Module is a navigation link in the application menu.

questions.question: Which of the following chart types can be used to represent individual values as bars and the cumulative total as line?
questions.explanation: A Pareto chart combines bars and a cumulative line to show the relative contribution of each category. It's based on the 80/20 principle and helps identify which categories contribute most to a total. Pivot Tables display data in a matrix format, Bar charts show simple comparisons, and Pie charts show proportions of a whole.

questions.question: Which of the following are the 3 key attributes for a field?
questions.explanation: The 3 key attributes for a field are Label (the user-friendly display name shown on forms), Name (the backend/database column name used in scripts and APIs), and Value (the actual data stored in the field). ID, Text, and Unique ID are not standard field attributes in ServiceNow's data dictionary.

questions.question: What defines which fields appear in a list and order of fields?
questions.explanation: A View defines which fields appear in a list and the order in which they are displayed. Administrators can create multiple views for the same table, each showing different columns. Users can switch between views using the list header context menu. Views can also be assigned to specific roles so different users see different columns.

questions.question: In the context of Flow Designer, which of the following are examples of ServiceNow core actions?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, B, D, E: Wait for Condition and Delete Record and Ask for Approval and Repeat. Options like "Schedule job" and "Activate Plugin" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: You are designing an email notification to be sent to the manager of the "Assigned to" user. Which feature is useful to specify the recipient field?
questions.explanation: Dot walking is the technique to reference fields on related records through a reference field. To send a notification to the manager of the 'Assigned to' user, you dot-walk: assigned_to.manager.email. This traverses from the current record → Assigned to user → that user's Manager → Manager's email address. No scripting is needed — just use dot notation in the notification's 'Who will receive' field.

questions.question: You are designing a form. Which of the following is useful if you need to allow fields to be populated automatically?
questions.explanation: To automatically populate fields on a form, you should use a Template. Templates pre-fill field values when creating new records, saving time and ensuring consistency. List View and Form View control how data is displayed but don't auto-populate fields. UI Policies change field behavior (mandatory/read-only/visible) but don't fill in values.

questions.question: The benefit of the activity stream inline editor is that you can add comments to tasks without opening them.
questions.explanation: True. The activity stream inline editor allows you to add comments and work notes to tasks directly from the list view without opening the full record. This speeds up bulk processing — agents can update multiple tasks quickly by typing in the inline editor rather than navigating into each record individually.

questions.question: The ______ is the view that agents use to work on issues with in-depth record information and suggestions about how to resolve issues.
questions.explanation: The Record view (also called the form view in Agent Workspace) is where agents work on issues with in-depth record information, related lists, AI-suggested solutions, and contextual side panels. It provides a comprehensive single-pane view for resolving tasks. Case view, List view, and Detail view serve different display purposes.

questions.question: The impersonate feature is not recommended because there is no way to know what actions the impersonator took on behalf of the impersonated user.
questions.explanation: False. The impersonate feature IS recommended for testing and troubleshooting because all impersonation actions are logged in the system. Administrators can see exactly what the impersonator did via System Logs > Impersonation Log. The audit trail ensures accountability, making impersonation a safe and recommended practice for testing role-based access.

questions.question: ServiceNow instance is single-tenant.
questions.explanation: True. ServiceNow instances are single-tenant, meaning each customer gets their own dedicated instance with its own database, application server, and URL. Unlike multi-tenant platforms where customers share resources, single-tenancy ensures data isolation, independent upgrade schedules, and customization freedom without affecting other customers.

questions.question: A data policy defined for a table will only run when data is inserted through the form, but it will not run when the data is inserted via import set.
questions.explanation: False. A Data Policy applies enforcement regardless of how data enters the system — through forms, import sets, web services, or scripts. Unlike UI Policies (which only run on forms), Data Policies enforce field rules at the server level, ensuring data integrity even when records are modified programmatically or via integrations.

questions.question: The ServiceNow platform uses a single system of record and a common data model.
questions.explanation: True. The ServiceNow platform uses a single system of record (one database for all applications) and a common data model (shared tables like Task, CMDB, sys_user). This means Incident, Problem, Change, and other applications share the same underlying data structure, enabling seamless cross-application reporting and automation.

questions.question: What does it mean if the "Match all" checkbox is checked in the User Criteria form?
options: This user criteria includes all the users with any roles
Any users in the users list of the user criteria is granted permission
All the elements of the user criteria form are mandatory
The user must meet at least one element of the criteria to be granted permission
The user must meet all criteria to be granted permission
questions.explanation: When the 'Match all' checkbox is checked in User Criteria, the user must meet ALL specified criteria to be granted access. Without it checked, meeting ANY single criterion is sufficient. For example, if criteria specify both a role and a group, 'Match all' requires the user to have that role AND be in that group.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid options in the "When" field in the business rule form?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are B, C, D, F: Before and Display and After and Async. Options like "Sync" and "In Parallel (Async)" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the Dependency View?
options: Dependency Views display all the configuration items that can be impacted by a change
Dependency Views display all the incidents that are linked to a change
Dependency views display a list of all configuration items in a CMDB
Dependency Views display the configuration items and the business services that it is part of and that it supports
questions.explanation: The Dependency View displays the configuration items (CIs) and their relationships in a graphical, hierarchical format. It shows upstream and downstream dependencies of a selected CI, helping IT teams understand the impact of changes or outages. For example, viewing a server's dependency view shows which applications, services, and business processes depend on it.

questions.question: The disadvantage of enabling the virtual agent is that some users would prefer to speak to a human agent.
questions.explanation: False. Virtual Agent actually benefits all users — those who prefer self-service get instant automated help, while those who prefer human agents can still be routed to live support via the 'Connect to Agent' option. Virtual Agent reduces wait times and handles routine requests, freeing human agents for complex issues.

questions.question: How to make a notification subscribable?
options: Select the checkbox "Allow personalization" in the notification form.
Select the "Subscribable" checkbox in the notification form
All members of groups that is specified in the "Who will receive" can subscribe to the notifications
Change the notification privacy type to "Public"
There is nothing that you need to do. All notifications are subscribable by default.
questions.explanation: To make a notification subscribable, select the 'Subscribable' checkbox in the notification record. This allows end users to opt in or out of receiving that specific notification through their notification preferences. Only notifications marked as subscribable appear in user preference settings. This gives users control over which alerts they receive.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid data sources for import sets?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, B, C, D, E: JDBC and XML FILES and HTTP and CSV FILES and EXCEL FILES.

questions.question: What is a Configuration Item?
options: Any record that refers to configuration or settings
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services
Any configuration record that determines the behavior of the database
Any component in ServiceNow is considered a configuration item
questions.explanation: A Configuration Item (CI) is any component in the IT infrastructure that needs to be managed to deliver services — servers, applications, network devices, databases, and business services. CIs are stored in the CMDB with attributes (name, class, status) and relationships (depends on, used by) that map the IT environment.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains the difference between Work Notes and Additional Comments?
options: Work Notes are only available to fulfillers whereas Additional Comments are only available to customers
Additional Comments are only available to fulfillers whereas Work Notes are available to both
Work Notes are only available to fulfillers whereas Additional Comments are available to both fulfillers and customers
Work Notes are stored in the activity history whereas Additional Comments are not
Additional Comments are stored in the activity history whereas Work Notes are not
questions.explanation: The key difference between Work Notes and Additional Comments is visibility: Work Notes are only visible to fulfillers (internal IT staff), while Additional Comments (Customer visible) are visible to both fulfillers and customers/requesters. Work Notes are for internal discussion; Additional Comments communicate with the end user.

questions.question: Which of the following knowledge base workflows immediately retires an article without needing an approval?
questions.explanation: The Knowledge - Instant Retire workflow immediately retires a knowledge article without requiring an approval process. The standard retirement workflow (Knowledge - Retire) routes through approvers before retiring. Instant Retire is useful when articles contain outdated or incorrect information that needs to be removed from public view immediately.

questions.question: You need to add a button to one of your forms. Which of the following should you use?
questions.explanation: To add a button to a form, use a UI Action. UI Actions create buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists. They can run client-side scripts, server-side scripts, or both. You configure the label, conditions for when it appears, and the action it performs. Form Layout controls field arrangement; Formatters display special widgets; UI Policies control field behavior.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding configuration items?
options: Software applications and business services are considered configuration items
Configuration items can be tangible or intangible
Relationship can be built between configuration items
CMDB consists of a static list of configuration items
questions.explanation: The statement that is NOT true is: 'CMDB consists of a static list of configuration items.' The CMDB is NOT static — it's a living, dynamic database that's continuously updated through Discovery, import sets, and integrations. CIs are added, modified, and retired as the IT infrastructure evolves. All other statements about CMDB relationships and classification are true.

questions.question: You are importing data from an excel sheet into the Incident table and want to make sure the import doesn't result in duplicate records. What should you do?
options: Uncheck the "Allow Duplicates" checkbox in the Transform Map form
Add a new record in the Compare related list
Set the coalesce to Title field
Add a business rule to run after insertion
questions.explanation: When importing data and you want to update existing records instead of creating duplicates, you should set the coalesce field (e.g., Title or Number) in the Transform Map. Coalescing checks if a record with that value already exists — if yes, it updates; if no, it creates new. This prevents duplicate records during repeated imports.

questions.question: Which of the following formatters is used to display the different stages in a linear process flow?
questions.explanation: The Process Flow Formatter displays the different stages in a linear process flow on a form. It shows a visual bar with stages (like New → In Progress → Resolved → Closed for incidents) so users can see where a record is in its lifecycle. It's added to a form via Form Layout as a formatter, not a regular field.

questions.question: Which of the following features helps users see reasonable relationships between configuration items?
questions.explanation: The CI Relationship Editor helps users see and manage reasonable relationships between configuration items. It provides a visual interface for viewing, creating, and modifying CI relationships in the CMDB. The Dependency View shows upstream/downstream dependencies in a read-only view, while the CI Relationship Editor allows active editing of relationships.

questions.question: The Import Set Table acts as a staging table, but the data will eventually be stored somewhere else.
questions.explanation: The Import Set Table acts as a staging area for imported data. Data is first loaded into this temporary table, then Transform Maps move it to the actual target table (e.g., Incident, User, CMDB). This two-step process allows data validation, cleaning, and mapping before it reaches production tables. Staging data is typically cleaned up after successful import.

questions.question: Having an up-to-date CMDB has a lot of benefits. Which of the following is particular NOT a benefit?
options: Facilitating quick analysis of change impact
Locating failed changes and associated incidents
questions.explanation: An up-to-date CMDB provides benefits like: accurate impact analysis, faster incident resolution, better change risk assessment, and compliance reporting. The option that is NOT a benefit would be something unrelated to configuration management — such as automatic code deployment, financial forecasting, or marketing analytics, which are outside the CMDB's scope.

questions.question: What is a common way of testing functionality for different roles?
questions.explanation: Impersonating a user is a common way to test functionality for different roles. By impersonating users with different roles (admin, ITIL, ESS), you can verify that security rules, UI policies, and access controls work correctly without needing separate login credentials. All impersonation actions are logged in the system for audit compliance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of knowledge base contextual search?
options: In the service portal, you can search for articles using the search text box
When viewing a knowledge base article, it will show you similar articles
When creating an incident, it will suggest relevant articles
questions.explanation: Contextual search in a Knowledge Base means the search is filtered based on the user's current context — for example, when creating an incident, Knowledge articles related to the selected category are automatically suggested. This helps users find relevant solutions without manual searching. It's configured through Knowledge Base properties and search contexts.

questions.question: Which of the following UI Actions is useful if you would like to apply the "Save As" functionality?
questions.explanation: The Insert and Stay UI Action provides 'Save As' functionality — it creates a new record with the current form values while keeping you on the form. This is useful for creating multiple similar records quickly. The regular Save button saves changes to the current record, while Insert and Stay copies field values into a brand new record.

questions.question: What is the Task table name?
questions.explanation: The Task table name is simply task. It is the base table that many other tables extend from, including incident, problem, change_request, sc_req_item, and sc_task. The task table provides common fields like number, state, assigned_to, priority, and short_description that all child tables inherit.

questions.question: Which table is used to store groups data?
questions.explanation: Groups in ServiceNow are stored in the sys_user_group table. This table contains all group records with fields like name, description, manager, email, type, and parent group. Users are associated with groups through the sys_user_grmember (Group Members) table, which creates the many-to-many relationship between users and groups.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding fulfiller and approver users?
options: Fulfiller users only have the approver_user role
Fulfiller users only have the itil role
Approver users have the itil and approver_user roles
Approver users only have the approver_user role
Fulfiller users have the itil and approver_user roles
questions.explanation: Fulfiller users have both the itil and approver_user roles. The itil role grants access to ITSM modules (Incident, Problem, Change) for resolving tasks. The approver_user role allows them to participate in approval workflows. Approver-only users just have approver_user. Having both roles means fulfillers can both work on tasks AND approve requests.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the difference between Save button and Update button?
options: Save applies the input validations before saving the record while Update skips the input validations
Save allows the user to remain on the same record while Update returns the user to the previously viewed record
Update allows the user to remain on the same record while Save returns the user to the previously viewed record
Save is used to insert new records while Update is used to update existing records
questions.explanation: The Save button saves the record and keeps you on the same form, while the Update button saves the record and returns you to the previously viewed list. Both buttons can be used on new or existing records — the key difference is navigation behavior, not insert vs update.

questions.question: How to show the visual task board view for tasks list?
options: Click on the gear icon in the top banner and select the checkbox "Show Visual Task Board"
Right-click on the list header and select "Show Visual Task Board"
Click on the gear icon in the tasks list and select the checkbox "Show Visual Task Board"
Right-click on any of the columns and select "Show Visual Task Board"
questions.explanation: To show the Visual Task Board view, right-click on any column header and select 'Show Visual Task Board'. This switches from list view to Kanban-style board.

questions.question: UI Policy is applied on all data input no matter what the channel is, including web form, import sets, etc.
questions.explanation: False — UI Policy only applies to the form interface. Data Policy applies to all channels including forms, import sets, and web services.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most accurate when it comes to how the system evaluates ACLs when a session requests accessing a record?
options: A user must pass both table and field ACL rules to access a record
A user must at least pass the table ACL rule to access the record
A user must pass either the table or the field ACL rules to access the record
A user must at least pass the field ACL rule to access the record
questions.explanation: When evaluating ACLs, a user must at least pass the table-level ACL rule to access a record. If they pass the table ACL but fail a field ACL, they can still see the record but that specific field will be restricted. If they fail the table ACL, they cannot access the record at all. ACLs are evaluated hierarchically: table → field → conditions/scripts.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to integrate flow designer with other instances and 3rd party applications?
questions.explanation: IntegrationHub integrates Flow Designer with external instances and third-party applications. It provides pre-built connectors and custom integration capabilities.

questions.question: What delivers a next generation, intuitive, personalized experience to drive productivity, improve engagement, and surface insights across the Now Platform?
questions.explanation: The Next Experience UI delivers a modern, personalized interface with unified navigation, AI-powered search, configurable workspaces, and improved productivity features.

questions.question: What is the minimum role needed to create import sets?
questions.explanation: The minimum role to create import sets is import_admin. Regular users and even ITIL users cannot manage imports without this specific role.

questions.question: Which table can be used to modify the configuration related to the maximum number of activities displayed in the history tab?
questions.explanation: System properties are stored in the sys_properties table. You can modify configuration settings like max active sessions by updating records in this table.

questions.question: Every record is identified by a 32-character, globally unique ID, which is called:
questions.explanation: Every ServiceNow record has a sys_id — a 32-character globally unique identifier. It's the primary key used internally to reference records across the platform.

questions.question: Which of the following roles is the minimum role required to be able to access My Work and My Group Work modules?
questions.explanation: The ITIL role is the minimum required to access My Work and My Groups Work modules. It's the standard fulfiller role for IT service management tasks.

questions.question: In ServiceNow fulfillment view, in which part of the screen do the forms get displayed?
questions.explanation: In the fulfillment view, forms are displayed in the Content Frame. The Banner Frame shows the header, and the Application Navigator is the left sidebar.

questions.question: Which form of storage is used to store data in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow uses a relational database (MySQL/MariaDB under the hood) to store all data. Tables, records, and relationships follow standard RDBMS principles.

questions.question: Which of the following can be useful if you want to restrict certain users from executing scripts on tables?
questions.explanation: ACLs are the correct tool for restricting specific users from executing reports on certain tables. They provide record-level security for report operations.

questions.question: Which of the following is useful when your users need to order more than one item together?
questions.explanation: An Order Guide bundles multiple catalog items together so users can order them as a set. Perfect when items are commonly ordered together.

questions.question: Which of the following is useful if you have a set of fields that needs to be used in multiple record producers?
questions.explanation: A Variable Set is a reusable collection of variables that can be shared across multiple catalog items. It avoids recreating the same variables on each item.

questions.question: Which of the following are supported types of client scripts?
questions.explanation: Supported client script types are: onChange (field value changes), onLoad (form loads), and onCellEdit (list cell edited). onAction and onMouseOver don't exist.

questions.question: Which section in the task form shows the full history of updates and comments made on the task?
questions.explanation: The Activity section on a task form shows the complete history of all updates, work notes, and comments made on the record in chronological order.

questions.question: ServiceNow instance can be hosted on the cloud or on-premises.
questions.explanation: False — ServiceNow instances are cloud-only. They cannot be hosted on-premises. ServiceNow is a SaaS platform hosted in ServiceNow's data centers.

questions.question: If a session requests access to data in a certain table, what happens if the user passes the table ACL rule but fails the field rule?
options: The user will be granted access to the table but won't see the field which he doesn't have access to
The user is denied access to the entire table
The user is granted access to the entire table because the table ACL rule will override the field ACL rule
questions.explanation: If a user passes the table ACL but fails the field ACL, they are granted access to the table but the specific field is restricted. Table access and field access are evaluated separately.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to define conditions that determine which users can create, read, write and retire knowledge base articles?
questions.explanation: User Criteria defines conditions that determine which users can create, read, or contribute to knowledge articles. It uses combinations of roles, groups, companies, and departments.

questions.question: If a table is extended but itself is not extending another table, it is called a:
questions.explanation: A table that is not extended from another table is called a base table. It sits at the top of the table hierarchy. Tables extending from it are child/extended tables.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding knowledge management workflows?
options: One workflow should be used for all knowledge bases
The same workflow that is used for publishing should be used for retirement
There are workflows available OOTB but you can create your own
None of the listed answers is correct
Workflows can be used only for publishing article but not for retirement
questions.explanation: There are OOTB workflows but you can create custom ones — ServiceNow provides default publishing workflows, but administrators can create and assign custom workflows to any knowledge base.

questions.question: Which application scope is used to identify applications created before application scoping?
questions.explanation: The Global application scope identifies applications created before application scoping was introduced. Legacy customizations default to the Global scope.

questions.question: ______ is a field where you can ask natural language questions about the trends and health of your processes.
questions.explanation: Analytics Q&A is a natural language interface where you type questions about data trends and get instant visualizations and answers from Performance Analytics data.

questions.question: What is a record producer?
options: Record producer is a form of automated test to allow data verification
Record producer is a scheduled job that creates records in table automatically
Record producer allows customers to fill a form that will be translated into a task-based record
Record producer allows fulfiller users to create records in the task table
questions.explanation: A Record Producer allows customers to fill a form that creates a record in a backend table (like Incident). It looks like a catalog item but creates records directly.

questions.question: You are designing a flow. You created an action on the incident record and you need to make use of this record in a subsequent action. Which of the following can be useful?
questions.explanation: Data pills in Flow Designer are dynamic references to values from previous steps in the flow. When you create an action on an incident record, the output data (like incident fields) becomes available as data pills that subsequent actions can use. Data pills are drag-and-drop references that resolve to actual values at runtime, enabling data flow between actions.

questions.question: A manager wants to view a snapshot of month end Sales performance data trended over time and forecasted into the future. What capability do you suggest?
options: Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Projection report
Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Trend report
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics captures data snapshots over time, enabling trend analysis, forecasting, and KPI tracking. It's the right tool for month-end trending reports.

questions.question: What are advantages of using Flow Designer?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer advantages: less manual scripting, reduces technical debt, smooth 3rd party integration, and complements the Integration Store. It doesn't support legacy workflows — it replaces them.

questions.question: When moving a homepage or dashboard between instances, what must you remember?
options: They are automatically added to the update set
Create a separate update set for them
They can be moved using ZIP files
They cannot be moved via XML
Manually add them to the update set
They cannot be moved via update set
questions.explanation: When moving homepages/dashboards between instances, you must manually add them to the update set. They are NOT automatically captured — this is a common gotcha.

questions.question: What policies are applied to all data entered into the platform: via form (UI), Import Sets, or Web Services?
questions.explanation: Data Policies apply to all data input channels: web forms, Import Sets, web services, and APIs. They enforce data quality regardless of how data enters the system.

questions.question: Which flow components allow you to specify when a flow should be run?
questions.explanation: Trigger and Condition components specify when a flow runs. The trigger defines the event (record created, scheduled, etc.) and conditions add filtering logic.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow resource can be used as a blueprint to map your IT Services to ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The Common Services Data Model (CSDM) is ServiceNow's blueprint for mapping IT services to the platform. It standardizes how services, applications, and infrastructure are modeled.

questions.question: You are creating a catalog item for ordering a new desktop computer with options for Color, RAM, Keyboard, and Monitor. How would you add these options?
questions.explanation: To add options to a catalog item, you add variables. Variables define the input fields — dropdowns for color, text fields for name, checkboxes for options, etc.

questions.question: Here is an example of the criteria: Companies: ACME North America; Departments: HR; Groups: ACME Managers; Match All: Yes. What user would have access?
options: Members of the ACME Managers group, and HR department, regardless of geography
Employee of ACME North America, who are members of HR Department or the ACME Managers group
Members of the ACME Manager group, who are also members of the HR Department and part of ACME North America
Users which are members of either ACME North America, or HR Department, or ACME Managers group
questions.explanation: This User Criteria evaluates as: members of ACME Manager group who are also members of the HR department at ACME North America. Groups criteria uses AND logic with other criteria.

questions.question: For a customer's inventory application, several inventory specifications fields are needed on an inventory ticket assigned to inventory support team members. How would you start to implement this?
options: Create inventory table as a new base Table. Then add inventory specifications fields, as needed
Create inventory table with fields. Then create view between the inventory and the Task table
Create inventory table with fields. Then create many to many relationships between inventory and the Task table
Create inventory table as an extended table from the Task Table. Then add the inventory specification fields, as needed.
questions.explanation: The best approach is to extend the Task table and add custom inventory specification fields. Extending Task inherits all task management features — assignment, SLAs, workflows, approvals, and state management — without rebuilding them. Creating a standalone base table misses these features. Views and M2M relationships don't provide the task management infrastructure needed.

questions.question: Which type of scripts run in the browser?
questions.explanation: UI Policies and Client Scripts run in the browser (client-side). All other options — Business Rules, Script Includes, ACL Scripts, Flow Designer Actions, Transform Maps — run server-side.

questions.question: What attributes you can manage using System Properties > Basic Configuration UI16
questions.explanation: Basic Configuration UI16 manages: Browser tab title, Base Theme, Module text color, Header background color, and Banner Image. Default calendar is not configurable here.

questions.question: A Service Catalog project will involve building 80 catalog items. Four fields will be mandatory on the forms. All of the other variables will be specific to the individual catalog item. What features would you use?
options: Create an Order Guide, which includes all variables, then copy and hide variables as needed
Create one Variable Set for the four variables, then add that variable set to each of the 80 catalog items
Create a Variable Set Template, then apply to all of the catalog items
Create a Record Producer that contains the four fields, then add to the record producer related list on the Catalog items
Create a Flow Designer Action, with Variable Set Data Pill, then apply flow to all of the 80 catalog items
questions.explanation: The best approach is to create one Variable Set containing the four mandatory fields, then add that Variable Set to each of the 80 catalog items. Variable Sets are reusable collections of variables that can be attached to multiple catalog items, ensuring consistency and reducing maintenance. If a mandatory field changes, you update the Variable Set once instead of 80 catalog items individually.

questions.question: A manager wants to run a report showing how many Service Requests have been fulfilled for Business Cards, since the beginning of the year. What table would they select?
questions.explanation: The Requested Item [sc_req_item] table stores individual items from a service request. To report on how many Business Card requests were fulfilled, you query sc_req_item filtered by the 'Business Cards' catalog item and state='Closed Complete'. The Request [sc_req] table is the parent order; Catalog Task [sc_task] tracks fulfillment work; Catalog Item [sc_cat_item] is the template definition.

questions.question: Which feature assists in understanding the Service Portal user experience better?
questions.explanation: User Experience Analytics helps understand how users interact with the Service Portal by tracking page views, search behavior, navigation patterns, and user journeys. It provides data on which portal pages are most visited, where users drop off, and how effectively they find information. Performance Analytics tracks KPIs but isn't specific to portal UX.

questions.question: Which operation is a record type access control list (ACL) that governs reports in dashboards and is enabled by default?
questions.explanation: report_view is the record-type ACL operation that governs whether users can view reports in dashboards. It is enabled by default, meaning users with appropriate roles can see reports. The security_admin role manages security configuration; pa_admin manages Performance Analytics; report_access is not a standard ACL operation name.

questions.question: Which role can administrators grant to users to view the configuration and execution details of only flows and subflows?
questions.explanation: The fd_read_flows role allows users to view the configuration and execution details of flows and subflows in Flow Designer without being able to edit them. fd_read is a broader read role; fd_read_operations allows viewing action configurations; fd_admin_designer grants full Flow Designer admin access including editing.

questions.question: Which Chatbot on the Now Platform allows you to send notifications directly to Slack and Microsoft Teams users?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is ServiceNow's chatbot that can integrate with Slack and Microsoft Teams to send notifications and enable conversational interactions. It uses Natural Language Understanding (NLU) to process user requests and can create incidents, check status, and provide KB articles directly within messaging platforms.

questions.question: When a flow runs an action, it generates a runtime value, which stays the same for the duration of the flow. What is the name of the runtime value?
questions.explanation: When a flow runs an action, it generates a Data pill runtime value — a dynamic reference to the action's output that remains constant for the duration of that flow execution. Data pills can be used in subsequent actions to reference these runtime values. They're the mechanism that passes data between steps in Flow Designer.

questions.question: What is contextual security in ServiceNow?
options: The contextual security manager profile provides flexibility and power to control information by controlling read/write authorization.
It doesn't apply the security rules to any level in the object hierarchy.
In platform security Settings, High automatically activities the contextual security plugin if is already active.
Protects a record based on its contents and table location, data is acted upon based on the position of the information in the table hierarchy. Defines access control rules to any level.
questions.explanation: Contextual security protects records based on their contents and table location within the hierarchy. It defines access control rules at any level in the object hierarchy, meaning data access is determined by the position of information in the table structure. This is different from role-based security, which is based solely on user roles regardless of record context.

questions.question: What are the three components of a filter condition?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are B, C, D: Field and Value and Operator. Options like "Table" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Which of the following can be configured by all users in the Next Experience instances?
questions.explanation: In Next Experience instances, all users can configure their Personalised Start Page. This allows each user to customize their landing page with widgets, favorites, and quick actions. Custom menus, AI Search configuration, and Admin menus require administrative roles. The Readiness Checker is an admin tool, not a user-configurable feature.

questions.question: Which role can manage multiple Knowledge bases?
questions.explanation: The knowledge_admin role can manage multiple Knowledge Bases, including creating bases, setting properties, managing workflows, and controlling access. The kb_admin role manages a single knowledge base. sn_kb_admin and knowledge_base_admin are not standard ServiceNow role names for this purpose.

questions.question: You can add human-readable keywords to the URLs of portal pages to improve SEO. What can be added?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, D: Dynamic page variables and Static content. Options like "Page parameters" and "Sys ID" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Which of the following roles cannot be delegated?
questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, D: admin and role_delegator. Options like "itil" and "user_admin" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: What is a best practice regarding data imports?
options: Plan time before your import to remove obsolete or inaccurate data
Use extremely large Import Sets, instead of multiple large Import Sets
Adjust your Transform maps, after the data is loaded into the target table
Create a new import set table for each new data load
Monitor data quality and clean imported data, using the Data Scrub Workspace
questions.explanation: The best practice for data imports is to plan time before your import to remove obsolete or inaccurate data. Clean data before importing reduces errors and cleanup work. Other best practices include: use reasonably sized import sets (not extremely large ones), test Transform Maps before loading to the target table, and reuse existing import set tables when possible.

questions.question: What process allows users to create, categorize, review, approve and browse important information in a centralized location?
questions.explanation: Knowledge Management is the process that allows users to create, categorize, review, approve, and browse important information in a centralized location (the Knowledge Base). It follows the Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) methodology. Self Service Management is a broader concept; Knowledge-Centred Management and Information Portal Management are not standard ServiceNow terms.

questions.question: Why is it recommended that you limit update sets to a maximum of 100 records?
options: Smaller update sets can be imported to production during business hours
Improve ability to troubleshoot issues with default update set
Make it easier to identify and review changes
questions.explanation: The correct answers are C, E: Reduce potential conflicts and Make it easier to identify and review changes. Options like "Comply with ISO audit requirements" and "Smaller update sets can be imported to production during business hours" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: What are the different ways to bring users into the ServiceNow system?
options: Through Single Sign-on, LDAP, Homepage Admin, manually entering users.
Through Single Sign-on, Knowledge Base, manually created by admin.
Through Knowledge Base, Organization Management process module, manually creating users.
Through Single Sign-on, LDAP, using an import sets (importing users), both manually entering users and creating users.
questions.explanation: Users can be brought into ServiceNow through: Single Sign-On (SSO) for federated authentication, LDAP integration for directory synchronization, Import Sets for bulk user imports from spreadsheets/databases, and manual creation by administrators via the User form. These methods can be used individually or in combination.

questions.question: Which one of the following are types of Service Catalog variables?
questions.explanation: Service Catalog variable types include: Select Box (dropdown with predefined choices), Check Box (true/false toggle), and Multi-line Text (large text input). Other variable types include Single-line Text, Reference, Date, Attachment, and more. Number List is not a standard variable type. Variables capture user input on catalog item forms.

questions.question: In a typical ServiceNow instance, what types of users are in the system?
options: 1) System Administrator 2) Delegate Administrator 3) ITIL User 4) ESS user
1) ESS user 2) Delegate Administrator 3) ITIL User 4) System Administrator
1) ESS user 2) ITIL User 3) Delegate Administrator 4) System Administrator
1) System Administrator 2) ITIL User 3) Delegate Administrator 4) ESS user
questions.explanation: User hierarchy from most to least access: ESS user → ITIL User → Delegate Administrator → System Administrator. ESS (Employee Self-Service) users have the least access.

questions.question: When using Transform Mapping, how we can dynamically map field?
options: We can dynamically map source and destination fields by using ServiceNow scripting objects and functionality.
By updating the fields using update sets, we can add/delete/modify the fields using rules and server scripts.
We cannot dynamically map source and destination fields using ServiceNow scripting objects and functionality.
We cannot Schedule data imports for mapping the source and destination fields.
questions.explanation: In Transform Mapping, you can dynamically map source and destination fields using scripts in the mapping record. This allows conditional and computed field mappings.

questions.question: By default in ServiceNow, what customizations are added to Update Sets?
questions.explanation: By default, changes made to forms (layout, field additions, UI policies) are captured in update sets. Data changes and homepage modifications must be manually added.

questions.question: An IT user calls the service desk because they need to work on task records but can only see Self Service on their homepage. What issues could explain this?
options: Their user account was not approved by their manager
Their user account does not belong to any groups, which contain the ITIL role
Their user account is not logged in properly
Their user account does not have ITIL role
questions.explanation: The correct answers are B, D: Their user account does not belong to any groups, which contain the ITIL role and Their user account does not have ITIL role. Options like "Their user account was not approved by their manager" and "Their user account is not logged in properly" are incorrect in this context.

questions.question: What is the industry term used to describe the computing platform and solution stack that supports the delivery of web applications?
questions.explanation: Platform as a Service (PaaS) describes the computing platform ServiceNow runs on. It provides the infrastructure, runtime, and tools for building applications.

questions.question: The ______ is a user friendly reference to a field and the ______ is the backend reference to a field.
questions.explanation: The label is user-friendly (displayed on forms), and the name is the backend reference (used in scripts and APIs). For example, label 'Priority' → name 'priority'.

questions.question: What features of ITIL are utilized by the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow utilizes ITIL features: Strategy, Design, Transition, and Operations. These align with the ITIL Service Lifecycle framework.

questions.question: What integration with Catalog Builder enables you to translate the content of the catalogue items on the Catalog Builder dashboard?
questions.explanation: The Localization Framework integrates with Catalog Builder to translate catalog content into multiple languages, supporting global deployments.

questions.question: Is it true that any user can have multiple roles but can only be part of single assignment group on ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: False — a user can have multiple roles AND be part of multiple assignment groups. There's no limit on either roles or group memberships.

questions.question: You can limit ServiceNow instance access by IP ranges?
questions.explanation: True — administrators can restrict instance access by IP ranges using IP Access Controls. This adds a network-level security layer.

questions.question: Two departments (HR and Facilities) need a way for employees to request event room setup services. Both have their own service catalogs. What do you do?
options: Create one catalog item for HR and one for facilities; then publish each to the appropriate catalog
Create one catalog item; then publish to the parent catalogue, which is accessible to both
Create one catalog item; then use ACLs to control access
Create one catalogue item; then publish to both catalogs
questions.explanation: Create one catalog item and publish to both HR and Facilities categories. This avoids duplication while making the item accessible in both departments' catalogs.

questions.question: What do you use in CMDB Workspace to verify the existence of actual IT infrastructure and applications that you own, systematically and in bulk?
questions.explanation: CI Attestation in CMDB Workspace verifies the existence of actual IT infrastructure. CI owners periodically confirm their CIs are accurate and up to date.

questions.question: Which module displays a list of tasks assigned to a user's group but not yet assigned to an individual user?
questions.explanation: My Groups Work displays tasks assigned to the user's group but not yet assigned to a specific individual. These are the unassigned group queue tasks.

questions.question: What can agents do with the Sidebar feature in the Next Experience UI?
options: Integrate with other Workspaces to display related records.
Create, open and search for discussions about their work
Have real-time collaboration with others from a Workspace interaction-based record
Broadcast a text message or initiate a conference call with other agents
questions.explanation: The Sidebar in Next Experience allows agents to create and search discussions and have real-time collaboration from a Workspace. It's the built-in collaboration tool.

questions.question: Which of the following operation is a record-type access control list that restricts access to reports based on a role?
questions.explanation: report_view is the record-type ACL that restricts access to reporting on specific tables. It controls who can generate reports from a table's data.

questions.question: What details can you find in the import set record after running an import?
questions.explanation: After running an import, the import set record shows: Import Log (success/error details), Import Set Runs (execution history), and Import Set Rows (individual row status).

questions.question: Which knowledge feedback option CANNOT be disabled at the knowledge base level?
options: All of them can be disabled
questions.explanation: All knowledge feedback options can be disabled at the knowledge base level — marking as helpful, commenting, flagging, and rating can all be turned off. None are permanently required.

questions.question: For Administrators creating new Service Catalog items, what is the characteristic they should know about Service Catalog variables?
options: Service Catalog variables can only be used in Record Producers
Service Catalog variables cannot affect the order price
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Order Guides
Service Catalog variables are global by default
questions.explanation: Service Catalog variables are global by default. This means they can be reused across multiple catalog items unless explicitly scoped to a specific item.

questions.question: Which of the following can be customized through the Basic Configuration UI 16 module?
questions.explanation: Basic Configuration UI16 allows customization of: System Date Format, Banner Image, and Browser Tab Title. These are the common branding and display settings.

questions.question: Which term best describes something that is created, has work performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed?
questions.explanation: A Task is something that is created, has work performed on it, and is eventually closed. Incidents, problems, changes, and requests all extend the Task table.

questions.question: What allows agents to initiate a group discussion from a Workspace task-based or interaction-based record?
questions.explanation: The Sidebar in Next Experience allows agents to initiate group discussions from a Workspace. It provides real-time collaboration alongside task records.

questions.question: What are the different Schema relationship types that are supported for tables?
questions.explanation: Schema relationship types: Referenced by (other tables reference this), Referencing (this table references others), Extending (this table extends a parent), and Extended by (child tables extend this).

questions.question: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?
options: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Workflows
Order Guides, Item Variables, and Workflows
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables
questions.explanation: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items. These are the three main catalog components accessible from the homepage.

questions.question: There is a business requirement to restrict incident reporting to specific roles for better governance. What access control operation should they use to allow viewing the contents of the reports on the incident table?
questions.explanation: The report_view ACL restricts incident reporting to specific roles. It controls who can create and view reports on the incident table.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct when referring to UI Actions?
options: UI Actions on the task table are not available to its extended tables
UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted
UI Actions are only executed on the server
Conditions can be specified to be determined when a UI Action appears
questions.explanation: UI Actions can have conditions specified to determine when they appear. Conditions can be field-based or scripted, and UI Actions can run both client and server scripts.

questions.question: Which feature enables you to maintain a unified content categorization across different content types, such as catalogue items, knowledge articles, and community posts?
questions.explanation: Taxonomy enables unified content categorization across different content types — knowledge articles, catalog items, and other resources share a common classification structure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a best example of Contextual Security in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: ACL is the best example of contextual security. ACLs evaluate access based on context — who the user is, what they're accessing, and under what conditions.

questions.question: Which one of the statements below describes the relationship between the incident table and task table?
options: The incident table is the parent of the task table
The incident table extends the task table
The task table extends the incident table
The task table is the child of the incident table
questions.explanation: The incident table extends the task table. Task is the parent, and incident inherits all task fields (assignment, SLA, work notes) plus adds incident-specific fields.

questions.question: Which of the below components runs on server side on ServiceNow instance? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Server-side components: Script Include, Business Rule, and Data Policy. UI, UI Policy, and Client Script all run in the browser (client-side).

questions.question: From the below options, please choose the correct definition of "inactivity monitor" in ServiceNow instance.
options: It is used to enhance the system logs. It provides more information on the duration of transactions between the client and the server.
It triggers an event for a task record if the task is inactive for a certain period of time. If the task remains inactive, the monitor repeats at regular intervals.
questions.explanation: An inactivity monitor triggers an event for a task record if the task hasn't been updated within a specified time period. It's used for SLA escalation and stale ticket management.

questions.question: Does ServiceNow support table rotation?
questions.explanation: Yes — ServiceNow supports table rotation, which archives older records to separate tables to maintain performance on active tables.

questions.question: Which of the following statements holds true for Service Catalog categories?
options: Users with the admin or catalog_admin roles can view categories only if there is an active item in the category and Availability is set to either Desktop or Both.
Users with the admin or cat_admin roles can view categories only if there is an active item in the category and Availability is set to either Desktop or Both.
questions.explanation: Users with the admin or catalog_admin roles can view categories in the Service Catalog. These roles provide full catalog management capabilities.

questions.question: What purpose does Client Transaction Time plugin serve in ServiceNow?
options: It enables to log a message in ServiceNow.
It enhances the system logs by providing additional information about the durations of transactions.
questions.explanation: The Client Transaction Timing plugin enhances system logs by providing additional client-side performance data — network time, browser rendering time, and server processing time.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about ServiceNow LDAP?
options: ServiceNow LDAP has only read access to customers AD
ServiceNow LDAP has read and write access to customers AD
questions.explanation: ServiceNow LDAP has only read access to customer directory servers. It can import user data but cannot write back to the LDAP directory.

questions.question: Where are customizations done on ServiceNow instance stored?
questions.explanation: Instance customizations are stored in sys_update_xml. This table contains the XML representation of every customization, linked to its respective update set.

questions.question: What is the sequence of conditions in a ServiceNow SLA definition?
questions.explanation: The SLA condition sequence is Start, Pause, Stop. Start begins tracking, Pause temporarily halts the clock (e.g., on hold), and Stop ends the SLA timer.

questions.question: Which of the below roles is required to manage UI policies?
questions.explanation: The ui_policy_admin role is required to manage UI policies. Without this role, users cannot create, modify, or delete UI policy records.

questions.question: Which role will a user require to initiate the setup of Agent Intelligence?
questions.explanation: Setting up Agent Intelligence requires the admin or ml_admin role. ml_admin is the specialized role for managing machine learning features in ServiceNow.

questions.question: You are navigating a ServiceNow instance and need to understand the core platform structure. Which of the following BEST describes the ServiceNow architecture?
options: ServiceNow runs on a monolithic database with all tables stored in a single namespace
ServiceNow uses a multi-tenant cloud architecture where each customer instance is completely isolated with no shared code
ServiceNow uses a multi-tenant architecture with shared code deployed across all instances, while data remains isolated per customer
ServiceNow requires on-premises deployment for enterprise customers and cloud-only for small businesses
questions.explanation: ServiceNow uses a multi-tenant architecture with shared code and isolated data. All instances run the same codebase/platform version (shared code), while each customer's data is completely segregated (isolated data). This enables efficient updates deployed once for all instances while ensuring privacy and compliance. Why others are wrong: A) Monolithic single namespace is outdated architecture — ServiceNow is cloud-based SaaS. B) The code IS shared across tenants — that's the core benefit of SaaS. D) ServiceNow is cloud-only; on-premises deployment is not an option.

questions.question: A user reports that they cannot see the 'Service Portal' application in their ServiceNow workspace. Which of the following is the MOST likely reason?
options: The Service Portal application has been deprecated and removed from all Zurich instances
The user's role does not have the necessary permissions or the Service Portal app may not be activated in this instance
Service Portal is only available in the Japan release, not Zurich
Service Portal requires a separate license purchase beyond the platform license
questions.explanation: Application visibility in ServiceNow depends on two things: the application must be activated/enabled in the instance, and the user's role must have access permissions. If a user can't see Service Portal, the most common reasons are the portal isn't activated or the user lacks the required role. Why others are wrong: A) Service Portal is not deprecated in Zurich. C) Service Portal is available in all releases. D) It's included with the platform license — no separate purchase needed.

questions.question: You need to identify which module contains system administration and setup functions. Where would you navigate to manage users, roles, and system properties?
questions.explanation: System Administration → System Settings is the standard administrative hub for user management, role configuration, system properties, and security settings. Why others are wrong: A) Service Portal is for end-user requests, not administration. B) System Definition → Tables is for data modeling, not user/role management. D) Control Center is for dashboard/personalization, not core admin.

questions.question: When logging into a ServiceNow instance, you notice that the interface displays different options based on the user's role. What is this feature called?
questions.explanation: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is the security mechanism that determines what tables a user can access, what records they can see, and what actions they can perform. When users log in, ServiceNow loads their assigned roles and filters data/UI accordingly. Why others are wrong: B/C) Dynamic/Contextual Navigation describe how the menu adapts visually, but the underlying security mechanism is RBAC. D) Unified Interface is about UI presentation, not access control.

questions.question: You have been assigned to create a new user account for an employee who will be using the ITSM module. Which of the following is NOT a mandatory field when creating a user record?
questions.explanation: When creating a user record, ServiceNow requires User ID (unique identifier), First Name, and Last Name as mandatory fields. Middle Name is optional — it's a nice-to-have field but not required for the system to function. Why others are wrong: A, B, and C are all mandatory fields; the system will reject incomplete entries without them.

questions.question: Your organization needs to control which users can create incidents. You decide to implement Access Control Lists (ACLs). Which of the following BEST describes how ACLs evaluate permissions?
options: ACLs are evaluated from most specific to least specific; the first match wins
ACLs are evaluated alphabetically regardless of specificity
All matching ACLs are combined with AND logic
ACLs are only evaluated for admin users
questions.explanation: ServiceNow evaluates ACLs using specificity order — most specific match first, and the first match wins. This means a detailed ACL (e.g., for a specific field + role + condition) is evaluated before a generic one (e.g., table-level). This prevents generic rules from blocking specific exceptions. Why others are wrong: B) Evaluation is specificity-based, not alphabetical. C) AND logic is incorrect — the first match determines access. D) ACLs apply to all users, not just admins.

questions.question: You need to modify a form to make a field mandatory for all users. Which of the following would you use to achieve this?
questions.explanation: UI Policy is used for form appearance/behavior — making fields mandatory, read-only, or visible/hidden. It's the standard, no-code way to control form behavior. Business Rules handle data validation and backend logic. Why others are wrong: A) Business Rules execute after form submission — too late to enforce mandatory at the form level. C) Client Scripts work but UI Policies are simpler and purpose-built for this. D) Script Includes are backend code libraries, not for form behavior.

questions.question: A business requirement states that the 'Assignment Group' field on incidents should be read-only after the incident is assigned. Which configuration method would BEST achieve this?
options: A Business Rule with before insert trigger
A UI Policy that makes the field read-only based on the condition that status != 'Unassigned'
An ACL restricting the incident.assignment_group table
A Client Script with onLoad event handler
questions.explanation: This requires conditional form-level behavior (read-only based on status), which is exactly what UI Policies are designed for. Set the condition to status != 'Unassigned' and the action to make Assignment Group read-only. Why others are wrong: A) Business Rule with before insert fires at the wrong time and context. C) ACLs control table-level permissions, not individual field behavior. D) Client Script could work but is over-engineered — UI Policy is simpler.

questions.question: You want to create a group for the IT Service Desk team. Which of the following is a characteristic of groups in ServiceNow?
options: Groups can contain only users, not other groups
Groups can contain both users and other groups (nested groups)
Groups are deprecated in Zurich and replaced by teams
Groups can only be created via API, not through the UI
questions.explanation: Groups in ServiceNow are flexible organizational structures that can contain individual users AND other groups (nesting). For example, an 'All IT' group can contain 'Service Desk' and 'Infrastructure' sub-groups, allowing hierarchical organizational structures. Why others are wrong: A) Groups support both users and nested groups. C) Groups are not deprecated — they're the primary way to organize users. D) Groups can be created/managed via UI at System Administration → Users → Groups.

questions.question: Your system administrator wants to ensure that certain users cannot delete records from the Incident table. Which approach would you use?
options: Create a Business Rule with a before delete trigger that cancels the operation
Create an ACL with operation 'delete' on the incident table
Create a UI Policy that hides the delete button
Modify the form layout to remove the delete button
questions.explanation: To control who can delete records, use an ACL with the delete operation on the incident table. ACLs are table-level security controls that enforce permissions at the database level for Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations. Why others are wrong: A) Business Rules can intercept but ACLs are the proper security mechanism. C) UI Policy only hides the button cosmetically — users can still delete via API/backend. D) Form layout hiding is even weaker — only hides UI, doesn't prevent the action.

questions.question: You need to configure system properties for your instance. Where would you navigate to set global configuration values such as time format or email settings?
questions.explanation: System Administration → System Properties is where you configure global values like email settings, time format, default values, logging levels, and integration endpoints. These properties affect all modules and users instance-wide. Why others are wrong: A) System Definition is for data modeling. C) Control Center is for personal dashboards. D) 'System Settings → Global Properties' is not a valid navigation path.

questions.question: A workflow needs to automatically create a notification when a high-priority incident is assigned. What feature would you use to send notifications to users?
questions.explanation: Notification Rules are the standard feature for sending notifications based on table events. A Notification Rule defines When (table + event trigger), Who (recipients), and What (email subject/body). Why others are wrong: B) Event Handlers are backend event processors (older approach). C) Alert Triggers use deprecated terminology. D) Task Notifications is not the standard feature name.

questions.question: Your organization requires approval for all change requests above a certain risk level. Which of the following BEST describes how approvals work in ServiceNow?
options: Approvals are manual processes that must be completed outside the platform
Approvals are table records that track approval status and can be configured via approval rules
Approvals require custom scripting for every use case
questions.explanation: Approvals in ServiceNow are database records (in the Approval table) that track approval status and are routed to approvers based on Approval Rules. They support conditional approvals, delegations, and rejections — all within the platform. Why others are wrong: A) Approvals are fully in-platform, not external. C) They support email, in-app notifications, and Agent Workspace. D) Standard approvals are built-in and don't require custom scripting.

questions.question: You want to configure an approval workflow where a manager must approve a change request before it can proceed. Which of the following should you use?
options: Use the Approval feature in the Change Management module
questions.explanation: The Approval feature in Change Management handles approval workflows end-to-end. You create an Approval Rule, set the trigger condition (e.g., risk level), and specify approvers (manager, group, or role). The system auto-creates approval records and routes them. Why others are wrong: A) Task templates create task records, not approvals. C) Business Rules can't manage approval workflows. D) Workflow Editor is outdated — Flows and built-in Approvals are the current approach.

questions.question: A user reports that they are not receiving notifications for incident updates. You check the Notification Rules and they appear correct. What else should you verify?
options: The user's notification preferences might be disabled
Notification Rules only work for administrative users
Notifications are sent only via SMS, not email
The user must manually enable notifications on their device
questions.explanation: Even if Notification Rules are configured correctly, notifications won't send if the user's personal notification preferences are disabled or they've unsubscribed. Users can manage their notification settings in their user record. This is a common troubleshooting issue. Why others are wrong: B) Notification Rules work for all users, not just admins. C) Notifications support multiple channels including email. D) Notifications are automatic when both the rule and user settings are enabled.

questions.question: Your organization uses tasks extensively. Which of the following BEST describes what tasks are in ServiceNow?
options: Tasks are only used in the ITSM module
Tasks are a generic table structure that other modules extend for specific purposes like Incidents and Changes
Tasks cannot have child tasks or subtasks
Tasks are automatically created and cannot be manually modified
questions.explanation: Tasks are a fundamental, extensible table structure in ServiceNow. The base Task table has common fields (assigned_to, state, description, etc.), and other modules extend it: Incident extends Task, Change extends Task, Problem extends Task, Release extends Task. This inheritance model ensures consistent behavior across modules. Why others are wrong: A) Tasks are cross-module, not just ITSM. C) Tasks support subtasks and child tasks. D) Tasks can be manually created and modified.

questions.question: You are configuring a notification that should only be sent during business hours. Where would you set this condition?
options: In the Notification's scheduled time settings
This is not possible in ServiceNow
questions.explanation: To send notifications only during business hours, set a time-based filter condition in the Notification Rule (e.g., current time >= 9 AM AND current time Why others are wrong: B) Scheduled time settings don't have business hour logic. C) User preferences control personal notification toggles, not time-based rules. D) ServiceNow absolutely supports time-based conditions.

questions.question: Your organization wants to show a comment on an incident form that reminds technicians to check for duplicates before assigning. This comment should appear when the incident is first opened. What would you use?
options: A Business Rule with 'Display in form' option
A UI Policy with a 'Show message' action
A Client Script with an onLoad event
An HTML field on the form with static text
questions.explanation: To display a message on a form when it loads, use a UI Policy with a 'Show message' action. UI Policies can run on onLoad events, trigger based on conditions, and display instructional messages — perfect for reminders like 'check for duplicates.' Why others are wrong: A) Business Rules don't display form messages. C) Client Script could work but UI Policy is simpler and purpose-built. D) Static HTML fields aren't conditional and clutter the form.

questions.question: When configuring approvals, you need to specify who should approve a change request. Which of the following can be configured as an approver?
options: Individual users, groups, or users specified by a template
questions.explanation: Approval Rules in ServiceNow are flexible and can specify approvers as individual users (by name), groups (entire group), or templates (users matching a role, manager relationship, or other criteria). For example: 'all users with Change Manager role' or 'requesting user's manager.' Why others are wrong: A) Only individual users is too limited. B) Only groups is too limited. D) Not restricted to just the Change Manager role.

questions.question: A business rule needs to send a notification when an incident is created with severity 1. What type of Business Rule trigger would you use?
questions.explanation: Sending a notification when an incident is created requires an after insert trigger. At this point the incident is saved to the database and can be referenced by notifications. Why others are wrong: B) Before insert is too early — the incident isn't in the database yet. C) After update fires on modifications, not creation. D) Before delete is for deletion events, completely unrelated.

questions.question: You need to create a workflow where multiple approvers must approve a change request sequentially. What approval configuration would support this?
options: A single approval with multiple recipients
Multiple approval workflow steps configured in sequence
Individual approvals cannot be sequential; they must be parallel
questions.explanation: For sequential (one-by-one) approvals, create multiple approval workflow steps in sequence. Step 1 routes to Approver A and waits for their response; only after approval does Step 2 route to Approver B. Why others are wrong: A) A single approval with multiple recipients sends to all simultaneously (parallel). C) Sequential approvals ARE supported. D) Standard sequencing is possible without custom scripting.
